# Papercut strategy

These notes decide what a reel says and why it holds attention. The other papercut skills decide how it is written, staged and built. The rules come from studying high-performing faceless tech reels and from reading platform insights after posting. Keep your own evidence in the series' `research/analytics/`.

## Preflight

- Install: Minimal is enough. No library needed.
- Find the series folder and read its `SERIES.md` first. It holds the audience (who, level, regions to aim for and avoid), voice, palette and mascot notes, the visual style, the keyword log and what has worked so far. If it is missing, ask the user for those fields and write the file.
- For a competitor study: `yt-dlp`, `ffmpeg` and any speech-to-text tool. For an autopsy: the platform's insights numbers from the user.

## 1. Topic

- Re-skin proven winners. A topic that worked (for you or a competitor) in a new familiar format beats a new topic in a plain format. Example: a reel about running several AI agents as a council, remade as "a jury of 12 AIs puts your idea on trial".
- The viewer must be able to use the outcome. If they can't do anything with it, skip it.
- Something to give away: every winner promises a free skill, prompt, template, cheat sheet or setup by DM.
- Speed on a hot repo. The first reel on a trending repo takes most of the views. Ship within a day or two, on an angle the earlier reels didn't use (`../papercut-hook/references/hook-patterns.md`).
- Demand signals: competitor outliers (likes at 5x or more of their median), trending repos (stars per day), front-page threads, same-day launches. Save candidates to the series' idea backlog.

## 2. Format

Pick one familiar real-world format for the whole reel before writing a word: courtroom, pitch show, cooking show, heist movie, nature documentary, dating show, character-select screen, boss fight, job interview, Olympic podium. The viewer gets the premise in a second and every set and gag comes from it. A plain list of facts has no premise to grasp, so it gets less attention than the same facts told inside a format. The bank, with the story each format carries, is `../papercut-script/references/comedy.md`.

## 3. Audience level

Write at the level `SERIES.md` sets. There is no default audience. The feeling to leave behind: you're not behind, and now you know something most people don't.

## 4. Funnel and caption

- Spoken CTA: "Good thing I made [freebie]. For the link, comment KEYWORD." One short keyword tied to the topic.
- Deliver the freebie by DM with whatever comment-to-DM tooling the account allows. Keep sends slow and spaced, because platforms rate-limit bursts.
- Caption: the hook as the first line, a follow line so the DM lands, "READ BELOW" with the useful part written out, one send prompt ("Send this to the friend who..."), 3-5 hashtags.
- Shares matter most to the algorithm. A funny or useful reel gets sent.

## 5. Write the BRIEF

Put this block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md`. `papercut-hook` and `papercut-script` read it.

```
BRIEF
Source:   <link(s)>
Claim:    <the one claim the video proves>
Role:     <who or what does the work vs who advises or approves>
Mode:     open-source drop | news launch / worth-it | feature unlock
Format:   <the one familiar format>
Audience: <level, copied from SERIES.md>
CTA:      <KEYWORD> -> <the freebie>
Length:   22-30 s
```

## 6. Competitor study (when the user shares reels)

Method, setup and the subagent prompt: `references/competitor-analysis.md`.
- One subagent per reel, up to 4 at a time. Each downloads the reel, extracts frames at 2 fps, transcribes it, applies the six-question hook check and returns a fixed-format report.
- Synthesise into a comparison table (likes and comments vs the creator's typical reel, age at fetch, look, length), what drove the outliers, what to borrow and what stays your difference.
- Save it to `research/analytics/YYYY-MM-DD-<creator>-reels.md`. One reel is noise; look for a pattern across 4 or more.

## 7. After posting: the autopsy

- At about 2 h and 24 h collect views, skip rate, average watch time, the retention curve, likes, comments, saves, shares, follows, traffic source, top countries and ages.
- Read them in this order: hook, topic, format, audience, timing. Fix the earliest thing that failed before touching later ones.
- If most viewers are gone by 3-5 s, or the skip rate is clearly worse than your own median, the hook failed. Run `papercut-hook`.
- Write `research/analytics/YYYY-MM-DD-autopsy.md` and update `SERIES.md` with what changed.

## Gate

- [ ] `SERIES.md` read; audience, regions and voice respected.
- [ ] Topic has a demand signal, a usable outcome and a freebie by DM.
- [ ] One format named in a line.
- [ ] Vocabulary and the DM match the audience level.
- [ ] BRIEF written; caption planned.

## Hand-off

Next is `papercut-hook`. It reads the BRIEF in `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` and writes the HOOK block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/papercut/STORYBOARD.md`. If the episode folder isn't scaffolded yet, create `research/` and `papercut/` by hand; `papercut-build` merges them when it scaffolds.
</skill-invocation>
</system-reminder>

--- README
# Papercut library

A Remotion kit for short vertical (9:16) explainer reels in a cut-paper style, plus the scripts around it. The kit has paper components, 24 backdrops, camera moves, scene transitions and film-look layers. The audio folder has 79 sound effects and 8 music beds, all synthesised in code. The scripts scaffold an episode, time it to a voiceover, mix the sound, render it and pull reusable pieces back into the library.

The idea is that an episode is mostly choosing and configuring. Whoever builds it (you, or an agent following `../skills/papercut-explainer/SKILL.md`) reads two short catalogs instead of the kit source, picks sounds and a music bed by name, reuses kit components and scene templates, and writes new code only for what the episode needs that the kit lacks.

## Layout

```
library/
  README.md  HARVEST.md  CHANGELOG.md
  env.sh                       sourced by the scripts; fills the env vars below from ~/.config/papercut-explainer/config.env
  new_episode.sh               scaffold <series>/episodes/NN-slug/ (template project + synced kit + node_modules)
  audio/
    CATALOG.md                 every SFX and bed preset, one line each (generated)
    engine.js                  Web Audio kit (noise, tone, pop, chime, pluck...) and one parametric music bed
    sfx/<name>.js              one file per effect, first line "// @sfx name | tags | sec | description | origin"
    beds/<preset>.json         music beds as data (bpm, instrument, chords, pattern, percussion...)
    render.mjs                 cues.json + bed -> public/audio/music.wav + fx.wav (loads only the SFX the cues use)
  papercut/
    CATALOG.md                 every kit export with its props and a doc line (generated)
    AGENT_BRIEF.md             the brief a scene agent gets (what to read, file ownership, QA loop)
    kit/                       the Remotion kit; copied into each project as src/lib/
      tokens.ts fonts.ts paper/ ui/ cast/ props/ scenes/    (scenes/ holds parametric scene templates)
    template/                  empty episode project (Root, PapercutVideo and scene.ts read episode.json)
    public/                    default paper textures, fonts and the backdrop images; copied into each project
    backdrops-src/             React sources of the code-drawn backdrops, for redrawing or tweaking them
    tools/                     textures.py (procedural paper textures)
    sync_kit.sh  stubs.py      re-sync the kit into a project; write scene stubs and index.ts from episode.json
  tools/
    build_vo.py                narration lines + timing -> voiceover.wav, captions.json, src/plan.json
    cues.py                    per-scene SFX rows -> tools/cues.json
    render.sh  render.py       cached per-scene render -> out/<name>.mp4
    mix.py  qa.sh  sheet.py    audio mix, QA stills and labelled contact sheets
    timing_md.py               writes the "Timing" section of STORYBOARD.md from plan.json
    capture.mjs                screenshot a web page for the kit's RealShot component
    placeholder_vo.py          silent (or macOS `say`) narration, so a reel can be timed with no TTS
    selftest.sh                scaffold + build the bundled example (../examples/hello-reel), typecheck, render SFX and a still
    catalog.py  harvest.py     regenerate the two catalogs; list what an episode should give back to the library
    dialogue_timeline.py       two-speaker dialogue -> timeline.json + vo.wav (no template for it ships here)
  voice/                       optional local voiceover pipeline, see voice/README.md
```

## Quick start

Prerequisites.

- Node 20 or newer, and npm.
- ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH. `rsync` for the kit sync.
- Python 3.10 or newer with numpy and Pillow (textures and contact sheets) and soundfile (audio mix).
- Chrome or Chromium for the audio render and `capture.mjs`. Set `CHROME_PATH` if it is not in a usual macOS or Linux location. Remotion downloads its own headless browser for video.
- Optional: Qwen3-TTS and a speech-to-text backend for the voice pipeline (`voice/README.md`). Without them you can use `placeholder_vo.py`, or record the narration yourself.

Setup.

```
git clone <this repo>
export PAPERCUT_LIB="$PWD/library"
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Scaffold a new papercut episode from the shared library.
#   usage: new_episode.sh <series dir> <NN-slug> <CompositionId> [out-name]
#   e.g.   new_episode.sh ~/videos/my-series 04-mcp McpPapercut mcp-papercut
# Creates <series>/episodes/<NN-slug>/{research,narration/voice,papercut}. An existing episode folder is fine (the earlier stages
# write research/, narration/script.json and papercut/STORYBOARD.md there); files already present are never overwritten.
# The papercut project is the template plus the
# synced kit. node_modules comes from $DONOR, else from the newest <series>/episodes/*/papercut/node_modules (an APFS clone
# on macOS when the filesystem allows it, a plain copy otherwise), else from `npm i`.
set -euo pipefail

# realpath without GNU coreutils (macOS ships none)
rp() { python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "$1"; }

if [ $# -lt 3 ]; then echo "usage: $0 <series dir> <NN-slug> <CompositionId> [out-name]" >&2; exit 2; fi
L=$(dirname "$(rp "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
CH=$(rp "$1"); SLUG=$2; COMP=$3; OUTN=${4:-${SLUG#*-}-papercut}
E=$CH/episodes/$SLUG; P=$E/papercut
# SYNCED.txt is written last (by sync_kit.sh), so a run that died halfway can be repeated
if [ -e "$P/src/lib/SYNCED.txt" ]; then echo "already scaffolded: $P" >&2; exit 1; fi
mkdir -p "$E/research" "$E/narration/voice" "$P"
rsync -a --ignore-existing "$L/papercut/template/" "$P/"   # never overwrites; rsync is a required dependency

DONOR=${DONOR:-}
if [ -z "$DONOR" ]; then
  DONOR=$(ls -td "$CH"/episodes/*/papercut/node_modules 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
fi
if [ -d "$P/node_modules" ]; then
  :   # left by an earlier run that stopped after the install
elif [ -n "$DONOR" ] && [ -d "$DONOR" ]; then
  cp -cR "$DONOR" "$P/node_modules" 2>/dev/null || { rm -rf "$P/node_modules"; cp -R "$DONOR" "$P/node_modules"; }
else
  (cd "$P" && npm i --no-audit --no-fund)
fi

if [ -d "$CH/papercut-assets" ]; then
  "$L/papercut/sync_kit.sh" "$P" "$CH/papercut-assets"
else
  "$L/papercut/sync_kit.sh" "$P"
fi

python3 - "$P/episode.json" "$COMP" "$OUTN" <<'PY'
import json, sys
p, comp, out = sys.argv[1:]; e = json.load(open(p)); e["comp"], e["out"] = comp, out; json.dump(e, open(p, "w"), indent=1)
PY
[ -e "$E/narration/build_timing.py" ] || cp "$L/voice/build_timing.py" "$E/narration/"
[ -e "$E/narration/script.json" ] || echo "[]" > "$E/narration/script.json"
echo "new episode: $E  (comp $COMP -> out/$OUTN.mp4)"
echo "next: research/facts.md -> narration/script.json -> voice/narrate.sh -> voice/finalize.sh -> episode.json scenes+banners -> papercut/stubs.py -> tools/build_vo.py"
echo "      (the two voice steps are optional; any TTS works if it produces the files voice/README.md lists)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# papercut-explainer installer. Asks how much you want to set up, then does only that.
#
#   ./install.sh                         interactive (asks for a mode)
#   ./install.sh --mode standard --yes   no questions
#   ./install.sh --doctor                check what is installed
#   ./install.sh --uninstall             remove the skill links this script made
#
# Modes
#   minimal   the skills only. Strategy, hook, script, storyboard and style prompts work; nothing renders.
#   standard  minimal + everything needed to render silent reels: dependency check, Remotion skills,
#             Python tools (numpy + Pillow + soundfile), a self-test render.
#   full      standard + local voiceover: Qwen3-TTS venv (~1.5 GB), model download (2.3-4.2 GB), word-timing ASR.
#   custom    choose each component.
#
# Options
#   --mode M              minimal | standard | full | custom
#   --components a,b,c    with --mode custom: skills,deps,remotion-skills,pytools,tts,verify
#   --target T            which agent harnesses to install for: auto (default: every one found on this machine,
#                         else claude) | all | a comma list, e.g. claude,codex,gemini. Names: see harnesses.sh
#                         (claude opencode codex gemini cursor copilot amp goose cline roo kilo zed droid warp
#                         augment junie openhands crush kiro qwen windsurf, or "agents" for the shared ~/.agents/skills)
#   --skills-dir DIR      where skills go (overrides --target with a single dir);
#                         the subagent goes in the sibling folder DIR/../agents
#   --project DIR         install into DIR (that harness's project folders, e.g. DIR/.claude/skills,
#                         DIR/.agents/skills) instead of user-wide
#   --claude-model M      model for the papercut-scene subagent in Claude Code:
#                         sonnet (default) | opus | haiku | inherit (use the session model) | a full model id
#   --opencode-model M    model for it in opencode: inherit (default) | provider/model-id
#   --agent-model T=M     the same for any other harness with file subagents (codex, gemini), e.g. codex=deepseek-flash
#   --copy                copy the skills instead of symlinking them (no live updates from this checkout)
#   --tts-model 1.7B|0.6B model size for the voice step (default 1.7B)
#   --with-clone          also download the voice-cloning model
#   --yes, -y             accept defaults, never prompt
#   --dry-run             print what would happen, change nothing
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
LIB="$ROOT/library"
CFG_DIR="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/papercut-explainer"
DATA_DIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/papercut-explainer"
export PAPERCUT_CONFIG="$CFG_DIR/config.env"
. "$LIB/env.sh"
export PAPERCUT_LIB="$LIB"   # this checkout wins over a stale path left in an older config file

MODE=""; COMPONENTS=""; TARGET="auto"; TARGET_EXPLICIT=0; SKILLS_DIR=""; SKILLS_DIR_EXPLICIT=0; PROJECT_DIR=""
COPY=0; YES=0; DRY=0
AGENT_MODELS="claude=sonnet"; MODEL_FLAGS=""
TTS_MODEL=1.7B; WITH_CLONE=0; DOCTOR=0; UNINSTALL=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --mode) MODE=${2:?--mode needs a value}; shift 2 ;;
    --components) COMPONENTS=${2:?--components needs a value}; shift 2 ;;
    --target) TARGET=${2:?--target needs auto, all or a comma list of harness names}; TARGET_EXPLICIT=1; shift 2 ;;
    --skills-dir) SKILLS_DIR=${2:?--skills-dir needs a value}; SKILLS_DIR_EXPLICIT=1; shift 2 ;;
    --project) [ -d "${2:?--project needs a folder}" ] || { echo "--project: $2 is not a folder" >&2; exit 2; }
               PROJECT_DIR="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --claude-model) MODEL_FLAGS="$MODEL_FLAGS claude=${2:?--claude-model needs sonnet, opus, haiku, inherit or a model id}"; shift 2 ;;
    --opencode-model) MODEL_FLAGS="$MODEL_FLAGS opencode=${2:?--opencode-model needs inherit or provider/model-id}"; shift 2 ;;
    --agent-model) MODEL_FLAGS="$MODEL_FLAGS ${2:?--agent-model needs NAME=MODEL, e.g. codex=deepseek-flash}"; shift 2 ;;
    --copy) COPY=1; shift ;;
    --tts-model) TTS_MODEL=${2:?--tts-model needs 1.7B or 0.6B}; shift 2 ;;
    --with-clone) WITH_CLONE=1; shift ;;
    --yes|-y) YES=1; shift ;;
    --dry-run) DRY=1; shift ;;
    --doctor) DOCTOR=1; shift ;;
    --uninstall) UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,/^set -euo/p' "$0" | sed '$d'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

. "$ROOT/harnesses.sh"
resolve_targets "$TARGET"

# Models for the scene agent. Defaults: Claude Code sonnet, everything else inherits the session model.
for kv in $MODEL_FLAGS; do
  case "$kv" in *=*) ;; *) echo "--agent-model needs NAME=MODEL (got: $kv)" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  h_known "${kv%%=*}" || { echo "--agent-model: unknown harness '${kv%%=*}'" >&2; exit 2; }
  valid_model "${kv%%=*}" "${kv#*=}" || { echo "bad model '${kv#*=}' for ${kv%%=*} (opencode needs provider/model-id; others a plain id or inherit)" >&2; exit 2; }
  AGENT_MODELS="$AGENT_MODELS $kv"
done

# Destinations: skills folders and subagent jobs, de-duplicated (many harnesses share ~/.agents/skills).
# --skills-dir overrides everything with one folder (legacy); --project uses each harness's project folders.
SKILLS_DIRS=(); AGENT_JOBS=()   # a job is "kind|dir|harness"
if [ "$SKILLS_DIR_EXPLICIT" = 1 ]; then
  SKILLS_DIRS=("$SKILLS_DIR")
  case "$SKILLS_DIR" in */.opencode/skills|*/opencode/skills) AGENT_JOBS=("opencode|$(dirname "$SKILLS_DIR")/agents|opencode") ;;
                        *) AGENT_JOBS=("claude|$(dirname "$SKILLS_DIR")/agents|claude") ;; esac
else
  for h in "${TARGET_LIST[@]}"; do
    if [ -n "$PROJECT_DIR" ]; then sd="$PROJECT_DIR/$(h_row "$h" | cut -d'|' -f3)"; ad="$(h_row "$h" | cut -d'|' -f6)"; [ -n "$ad" ] && [ "$ad" != "-" ] && ad="$PROJECT_DIR/$ad"
    else sd="$(h_field "$h" 2)"; ad="$(h_field "$h" 5)"; fi
    in_array "$sd" "${SKILLS_DIRS[@]+"${SKILLS_DIRS[@]}"}" || SKILLS_DIRS+=("$sd")
    kind="$(h_field "$h" 4)"
    if [ "$kind" != none ] && [ -n "$ad" ] && [ "$ad" != "-" ]; then
      job="$kind|$ad|$h"; in_array "$job" "${AGENT_JOBS[@]+"${AGENT_JOBS[@]}"}" || AGENT_JOBS+=("$job")
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -t 1 ]; then B=$'\033[1m'; G=$'\033[32m'; Y=$'\033[33m'; R=$'\033[31m'; N=$'\033[0m'; else B=""; G=""; Y=""; R=""; N=""; fi
say()  { printf '%s==>%s %s\n' "$B" "$N" "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '  %s[ok]%s %s\n' "$G" "$N" "$*"; }
miss() { printf '  %s[--]%s %s\n' "$Y" "$N" "$*"; }
bad()  { printf '  %s[!!]%s %s\n' "$R" "$N" "$*"; }
run()  { if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then printf '  (dry run) %s\n' "$*"; else "$@"; fi; }
interactive() { [ "$YES" = 0 ] && [ -t 0 ]; }
confirm() {  # confirm "question" default(y|n)
  interactive || { [ "$2" = y ]; return; }
  local hint="[Y/n]"; [ "$2" = n ] && hint="[y/N]"
  printf '%s %s ' "$1" "$hint"; read -r a
  case "$(printf '%s' "$a" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" in y|yes) return 0 ;; n|no) return 1 ;; *) [ "$2" = y ] ;; esac
}

SKILL_NAMES() { for d in "$ROOT"/skills/*/; do [ -f "${d}SKILL.md" ] && basename "$d"; done; }
ver_ge() { [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$2" "$1" | sort -V | head -1)" = "$2" ]; }   # ver_ge have need

# The scene agent is written as a copy per harness, so the model is the user's choice and each format is right.
# Claude Code, opencode, Codex and Gemini name models and tools differently; the repo keeps one source per format
# family (agents/papercut-scene.md for Claude, agents/opencode/ for opencode) and derives the Codex and Gemini files.
AGENT_MARK='papercut-explainer install.sh (generated)'
agent_with_model() {  # agent_with_model SRC MODEL: markdown, model line after name: (none for "inherit")
  awk -v model="$2" -v mark="$AGENT_MARK" '
    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print; next }
    fm == 1 && /^model:/ { next }
    fm == 1 && /^name:/ { print; if (model != "inherit") print "model: " model; next }
    fm == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 2; print; print "<!-- " mark ": rerun the installer to change the model -->"; next }
    { print }
  ' "$1"
}
agent_for_gemini() {  # Gemini validates frontmatter strictly: name, description, model only (no Claude tools:/effort:)
  awk -v model="$2" -v mark="$AGENT_MARK" '
    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print; next }
    fm == 1 && /^(name|description):/ { print; next }
    fm == 1 && $0 == "---" { if (model != "inherit") print "model: " model; fm = 2; print; print "<!-- " mark ": rerun the installer to change the model -->"; next }
    fm == 1 { next }
    { print }
  ' "$1"
}
agent_for_codex() {  # Codex subagents are TOML: name, description, developer_instructions (+ model, model_reasoning_effort)
  python3 -B - "$1" "$2" "$AGENT_MARK" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys
src, model, mark = sys.argv[1:4]
fm, body = re.match(r'---\n(.*?)\n---\n(.*)', open(src).read(), re.S).groups()
field = lambda k: (re.search(r'^%s:\s*(.+)$' % k, fm, re.M) or [None, None])[1]
instr = body.strip()
assert "'''" not in instr
out = ["# " + mark + ": rerun the installer to change the model",
       "name = " + json.dumps(field("name")), "description = " + json.dumps(field("description"))]
if model != "inherit": out.append("model = " + json.dumps(model))
if field("effort"): out.append("model_reasoning_effort = " + json.dumps(field("effort").strip()))
out.append("developer_instructions = '''\n" + instr + "\n'''")
print("\n".join(out))
PY
}
agent_render() {  # agent_render KIND SRC MODEL
  case "$1" in
    gemini) agent_for_gemini "$2" "$3" ;;
    codex)  agent_for_codex "$2" "$3" ;;
    *)      agent_with_model "$2" "$3" ;;
  esac
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- doctor
doctor() {
  say "papercut-explainer: status (target: $TARGET = ${TARGET_LIST[*]})"
  local n=0 t=0 L_SKILLS=0 L_STD=1 L_FULL=0
  local best=0 dir_n nskills misses=() complete=()
  for dir in "${SKILLS_DIRS[@]}"; do
    dir_n=0
    for s in $(SKILL_NAMES); do
      if [ -e "$dir/$s/SKILL.md" ]; then dir_n=$((dir_n+1)); else misses+=("skill $s not in $dir"); fi
    done
    n=$((n+dir_n)); t=$((t+$(SKILL_NAMES | wc -w)))
    [ "$dir_n" -gt "$best" ] && best=$dir_n
    if [ "$dir_n" = "$(SKILL_NAMES | wc -w | tr -d " ")" ]; then complete+=("$dir"); fi
  done
  nskills=$(SKILL_NAMES | wc -w | tr -d " ")
  # No explicit --target: Claude-only and opencode-only installs are both fine, so one complete location passes.
  if [ "$TARGET_EXPLICIT" = 0 ] && [ "$SKILLS_DIR_EXPLICIT" = 0 ] && [ "${#complete[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    ok "skills: $nskills/$nskills in ${complete[*]}"; L_SKILLS=1
  elif [ "$n" = "$t" ] && [ "$t" -gt 0 ]; then ok "skills: $n/$t in ${SKILLS_DIRS[*]}"; L_SKILLS=1
  else for m in "${misses[@]}"; do miss "$m"; done; bad "skills: $n/$t installed"; fi
  [ -f "$PAPERCUT_CONFIG" ] && ok "config: $PAPERCUT_CONFIG (PAPERCUT_LIB=$PAPERCUT_LIB)" || miss "config file missing ($PAPERCUT_CONFIG)"
  if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then v="$(node -v | sed 's/^v//')"; if ver_ge "$v" 20; then ok "node $v"; else bad "node $v (need 20+)"; L_STD=0; fi; else miss "node (need 20+)"; L_STD=0; fi
  command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "npm" || { miss "npm"; L_STD=0; }
  command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "ffmpeg" || { miss "ffmpeg"; L_STD=0; }
  command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "rsync" || { miss "rsync"; L_STD=0; }
  command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "python3 $(python3 -c 'import platform;print(platform.python_version())')" || { miss "python3"; L_STD=0; }
  local remo_found=0 d
  for d in "${SKILLS_DIRS[@]}" "$HOME/.claude/skills" "$HOME/.config/opencode/skills" "$HOME/.agents/skills" "$HOME/.gemini/skills" "$HOME/.cursor/skills"; do
    [ -f "$d/remotion-best-practices/SKILL.md" ] && remo_found=1
  done
  if [ $remo_found = 1 ]; then ok "remotion skills"; else miss "remotion skills (npx skills add remotion-dev/skills, see step_remotion)"; L_STD=0; fi
  if "$PAPERCUT_PY" -c 'import numpy, PIL, soundfile' >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "python tools: numpy + Pillow + soundfile ($PAPERCUT_PY)"; else miss "python tools (numpy + Pillow + soundfile)"; L_STD=0; fi
  if papercut_find_chrome >/dev/null; then ok "Chrome or Chromium (sound effects and music render)"; else miss "Chrome/Chromium (only the SFX and music render needs it)"; fi
  if "$QWEN_TTS_PY" -c 'import qwen_tts' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "voice: qwen-tts importable ($QWEN_TTS_PY)"
    if ls -d "$HOME"/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-*-CustomVoice >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "voice: CustomVoice model cached"; L_FULL=1; else miss "voice: no CustomVoice model in the Hugging Face cache"; fi
  else miss "voice: qwen-tts not installed (optional; ./install.sh --mode custom --components tts)"; fi
  for f in kit/paper/camera.tsx public/bg/backdrops/backdrops.json public/bg/textures/felt-fibre.mp4; do
    [ -e "$LIB/papercut/$f" ] && ok "library: $f" || { bad "library file missing: $f"; L_STD=0; }
  done
  local level="none (skills not installed)"
  if [ $L_SKILLS = 1 ]; then level="Minimal"; [ $L_STD = 1 ] && level="Standard" && [ $L_FULL = 1 ] && level="Full"; fi
  say "Install level: $level"
}

uninstall() {
  say "removing skill links made by this installer"
  local rec="$CFG_DIR/installed.txt"; [ -f "$rec" ] || { echo "nothing recorded in $rec"; return; }
  while IFS= read -r p; do
    [ -n "$p" ] || continue
    if [ -L "$p" ]; then
      case "$(readlink "$p")" in "$ROOT"/*) run rm "$p"; ok "removed $p" ;; *) miss "kept $p (link points elsewhere)" ;; esac
    elif [ -d "$p" ] && [ -f "$p/.papercut-installed" ]; then run rm -rf "$p"; ok "removed $p"
    elif [ -f "$p" ] && { grep -q "$AGENT_MARK" "$p" 2>/dev/null || cmp -s "$p" "$ROOT/agents/$(basename "$p")" 2>/dev/null; }; then run rm "$p"; ok "removed $p"
    elif [ -e "$p" ]; then miss "kept $p (not an unmodified copy from this installer)"; fi
  done < "$rec"
  run rm -f "$rec"
  echo "Left in place: $CFG_DIR/config.env, venvs under $DATA_DIR, Hugging Face model cache. Delete them by hand if you want the space back."
}

[ "$DOCTOR" = 1 ] && { doctor; exit 0; }
[ "$UNINSTALL" = 1 ] && { uninstall; exit 0; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- mode
if [ -z "$MODE" ]; then
  if interactive; then
    cat <<EOF
${B}papercut-explainer setup${N}

How much do you want to set up?

  1) Minimal   The skills only (hook, script, storyboard, strategy, style prompts).
               Nothing renders. Takes seconds.
  2) Standard  Minimal + render silent reels: dependency check, Remotion skills,
               Python tools, a self-test render.             ~0.7 GB, a few minutes.
  3) Full      Standard + local voiceover: Qwen3-TTS + word-timing ASR.
                                                              +4-6 GB (1.5 GB venv + model).
  4) Custom    Pick each component.

EOF
    printf 'Choose 1-4 [2]: '; read -r c
    case "${c:-2}" in 1) MODE=minimal ;; 2) MODE=standard ;; 3) MODE=full ;; 4) MODE=custom ;; *) echo "pick 1-4" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  else
    echo "no terminal to ask on: pass --mode minimal|standard|full|custom (and --yes)" >&2; exit 2
  fi
fi

C_SKILLS=0; C_DEPS=0; C_REMO=0; C_PY=0; C_TTS=0; C_VERIFY=0
case "$MODE" in
  minimal)  C_SKILLS=1 ;;
  standard) C_SKILLS=1; C_DEPS=1; C_REMO=1; C_PY=1; C_VERIFY=1 ;;
  full)     C_SKILLS=1; C_DEPS=1; C_REMO=1; C_PY=1; C_TTS=1; C_VERIFY=1 ;;
  custom)
    if [ -n "$COMPONENTS" ]; then
      for c in $(printf '%s' "$COMPONENTS" | tr ',' ' '); do
        case "$c" in skills) C_SKILLS=1 ;; deps) C_DEPS=1 ;; remotion-skills) C_REMO=1 ;; pytools) C_PY=1 ;; tts) C_TTS=1 ;; verify) C_VERIFY=1 ;;
          *) echo "unknown component: $c" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
      done
    else
      interactive || { echo "--mode custom needs --components or a terminal" >&2; exit 2; }
      confirm "Install the skills (links into ${SKILLS_DIRS[*]})?" y && C_SKILLS=1
      confirm "Check dependencies (node 20+, npm, ffmpeg, python3)?" y && C_DEPS=1
      confirm "Install the Remotion agent skills (npx skills add remotion-dev/skills)?" y && C_REMO=1
      confirm "Set up Python tools (venv with numpy + Pillow, for QA contact sheets)?" y && C_PY=1
      if confirm "Set up local voiceover (Qwen3-TTS + ASR; 4-6 GB of disk)?" n; then
        C_TTS=1
        printf 'Model size: 1) 1.7B better, 4.2 GB   2) 0.6B lighter, 2.3 GB  [1]: '; read -r m
        [ "$m" = 2 ] && TTS_MODEL=0.6B
        confirm "Also download the voice-cloning model (same size again)?" n && WITH_CLONE=1
      fi
      confirm "Run a self-test render at the end?" y && C_VERIFY=1
    fi ;;
  *) echo "unknown mode: $MODE" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

if [ "$MODE" != custom ] && interactive; then
  say "Plan ($MODE)"
  [ $C_SKILLS = 1 ] && echo "  - link the skills into ${SKILLS_DIRS[*]} (${TARGET_LIST[*]})"
  [ $C_DEPS = 1 ]   && echo "  - check node, npm, ffmpeg, python3"
  [ $C_REMO = 1 ]   && echo "  - install the Remotion agent skills (global)"
  [ $C_PY = 1 ]     && echo "  - create a Python venv with numpy + Pillow"
  [ $C_TTS = 1 ]    && echo "  - build a voice venv and download Qwen3-TTS $TTS_MODEL (~$([ "$TTS_MODEL" = 1.7B ] && echo 4.2 || echo 2.3) GB)"
  [ $C_VERIFY = 1 ] && echo "  - scaffold a throwaway project and render one still (npm install runs once)"
  confirm "Go?" y || { echo "cancelled"; exit 0; }
fi
[ "$MODE" = full ] && interactive && ! confirm "Full mode asks for a multi-GB model download. Keep model size $TTS_MODEL?" y && { echo "rerun with --tts-model 0.6B or --mode standard"; exit 0; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- steps
FAILED=""; SKIPPED=""; DONE=""
note_fail() { FAILED="$FAILED $1"; bad "$1 failed: $2"; }

step_config() {
  say "config"
  run mkdir -p "$CFG_DIR"
  if [ "$DRY" = 0 ]; then
    papercut_config_set PAPERCUT_HOME "$ROOT"
    papercut_config_set PAPERCUT_LIB "$LIB"
  fi
  ok "$PAPERCUT_CONFIG"
}

# The scene-builder subagent, one file per (format, folder) job from the harness table.
install_agents() {
  local job kind adir harness model asrc a ext adst agen ts; ts="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  for job in "${AGENT_JOBS[@]+"${AGENT_JOBS[@]}"}"; do
    kind="${job%%|*}"; adir="${job#*|}"; harness="${adir##*|}"; adir="${adir%|*}"
    model="$(agent_model "$harness")"; asrc="$ROOT/agents"; [ "$kind" = opencode ] && asrc="$ROOT/agents/opencode"
    ext=md; [ "$kind" = codex ] && ext=toml
    run mkdir -p "$adir"
    for a in "$asrc"/*.md; do
      [ -f "$a" ] || continue
      adst="$adir/$(basename "$a" .md).$ext"
      if [ "$kind" = codex ] && ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then miss "skipped the Codex agent file: python3 not found"; continue; fi
      agen="$(mktemp)"; agent_render "$kind" "$a" "$model" > "$agen"
      if [ -L "$adst" ]; then run rm "$adst"
      elif [ -e "$adst" ]; then
        if cmp -s "$agen" "$adst" || cmp -s "$a" "$adst"; then run rm "$adst"   # identical copy: refresh it
        elif grep -q "$AGENT_MARK" "$adst" 2>/dev/null; then run rm "$adst"   # an earlier run, maybe with another model
        elif confirm "$adst exists and differs from this checkout. Back it up and replace?" y; then
          run mkdir -p "$CFG_DIR/backups"; run mv "$adst" "$CFG_DIR/backups/$(basename "$adst" ".$ext").$ts.$ext"; miss "backed up to $CFG_DIR/backups"
        else miss "kept existing agent $(basename "$adst")"; rm -f "$agen"; continue; fi
      fi
      run cp "$agen" "$adst"; rm -f "$agen"
      [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || echo "$adst" >> "$CFG_DIR/installed.txt"
      ok "agent $(basename "$a" .md) ($kind, model: $model) -> $adir"
    done

}

step_skills() {
  local onedir
  for onedir in "${SKILLS_DIRS[@]}"; do
    say "skills -> $onedir"
    run mkdir -p "$onedir" "$CFG_DIR"
    local ts bak; ts="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; bak="$CFG_DIR/backups"

local ts bak; ts="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"; bak="$CFG_DIR/backups"
    for s in $(SKILL_NAMES); do
      local src="$ROOT/skills/$s" dst="$onedir/$s"
      if [ -L "$dst" ]; then
        run rm "$dst"
      elif [ -e "$dst" ]; then
        if [ -f "$dst/.papercut-installed" ] || diff -rq "$src" "$dst" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          run rm -rf "$dst"   # an earlier --copy install or an identical copy (npx skills add): refresh it
        elif confirm "$dst exists and differs from this checkout. Back it up and replace?" y; then
          # backups live outside the skills folder, so agents do not load them as duplicate skills
          run mkdir -p "$bak"; run mv "$dst" "$bak/$s.$ts"; miss "backed up to $bak/$s.$ts"
        else miss "kept existing $s"; continue; fi
      fi
      if [ "$COPY" = 1 ]; then run cp -R "$src" "$dst"; [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || touch "$dst/.papercut-installed"; else run ln -s "$src" "$dst"; fi
      [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || echo "$dst" >> "$CFG_DIR/installed.txt"
      ok "$s ($onedir)"
    done
  done
  install_agents
  [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$CFG_DIR/installed.txt" ] || sort -u "$CFG_DIR/installed.txt" -o "$CFG_DIR/installed.txt"
}

step_deps() {
  say "dependencies"
  local miss_any=0
  if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then v="$(node -v | sed 's/^v//')"; if ver_ge "$v" 20; then ok "node $v"; else bad "node $v, need 20+"; miss_any=1; fi
  else bad "node not found. Install Node 20+: https://nodejs.org or 'brew install node'"; miss_any=1; fi
  command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "npm" || { bad "npm not found (ships with node)"; miss_any=1; }
  command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "ffmpeg" || { bad "ffmpeg not found: 'brew install ffmpeg' or 'apt install ffmpeg'"; miss_any=1; }
  command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "rsync" || { bad "rsync not found (the kit sync uses it): 'brew install rsync' or 'apt install rsync'"; miss_any=1; }
  if papercut_find_chrome >/dev/null; then
    ok "Chrome or Chromium (sound effects and music render)"
  else miss "Chrome/Chromium not found: only the SFX and music render needs it (set CHROME_PATH or install Chrome); video renders do not"; fi
  command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "python3" || { bad "python3 not found"; miss_any=1; }
  if [ $miss_any = 1 ]; then note_fail deps "install the items above, then rerun with --mode custom --components deps,verify"; return 1; fi
}

step_remotion() {
  say "Remotion agent skills (${TARGET_LIST[*]})"
  command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1 || { note_fail remotion-skills "npx not found"; return 1; }
  # `npx skills` installs into each harness's own folder. Skip a harness that already has the skill where it reads skills.
  local h id udir done_ids=()
  for h in "${TARGET_LIST[@]}"; do
    id="$(h_field "$h" 7)"; udir="$(h_field "$h" 2)"
    [ -f "$udir/remotion-best-practices/SKILL.md" ] && continue
    [ -f "$HOME/.claude/skills/remotion-best-practices/SKILL.md" ] && [ "$h" = claude ] && continue
    in_array "$id" "${done_ids[@]+"${done_ids[@]}"}" && continue
    done_ids+=("$id")
    run npx -y skills@latest add remotion-dev/skills -g -y -a "$id" || note_fail remotion-skills "npx skills add failed for $id; run it by hand"
  done
  [ "${#done_ids[@]}" -gt 0 ] || ok "already installed"
}

step_pytools() {
  say "Python tools (numpy + Pillow + soundfile)"
  local V="$DATA_DIR/tools-venv"
  command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { note_fail pytools "python3 missing"; return 1; }
  run mkdir -p "$DATA_DIR"

    run python3 -m venv "$V" || { rm -rf "$V"; note_fail pytools "could not create a venv (on Debian/Ubuntu: apt install python3-venv, then rerun with --mode custom --components pytools,verify)"; return 1; }
  fi
  run "$V/bin/python" -m pip install -q -U pip numpy pillow soundfile || { note_fail pytools "pip install failed"; return 1; }
  [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || papercut_config_set PAPERCUT_PY "$V/bin/python"
  ok "PAPERCUT_PY=$V/bin/python"
}

step_tts() {
  say "local voiceover"
  local args="--model $TTS_MODEL --yes"; [ "$WITH_CLONE" = 1 ] && args="$args --with-clone"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  run bash "$LIB/voice/setup_tts.sh" $args || note_fail tts "see the output above; rerun: library/voice/setup_tts.sh"
}

step_verify() {
  say "self-test render"
  run bash "$LIB/tools/selftest.sh" || note_fail verify "self-test failed; run library/tools/selftest.sh to see why"
}

step_config

[ $C_PY = 1 ] && step_pytools
[ $C_TTS = 1 ] && step_tts

# Shared environment for the papercut library scripts. Source it; do not execute it.
#   . "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../env.sh"      (adjust the relative path)
#
# Reads the installer's config file, then fills defaults. Variables already set in the
# environment win over the file. Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS default).
#
#   PAPERCUT_LIB      this library folder
#   PAPERCUT_PY       python with numpy + Pillow (contact sheets, textures)   default: python3
#   QWEN_TTS_PY       python with qwen-tts installed (voice/narrate)          default: python3
#   ASR_PY            python with an ASR backend (voice/asr)                  default: python3
#   PAPERCUT_CONFIG   config file path   default: ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env

_pc_cfg="${PAPERCUT_CONFIG:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env}"

if [ -f "$_pc_cfg" ]; then
  while IFS='=' read -r _k _v || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
    case "$_k" in ''|'#'*|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) continue ;; esac
    eval "_cur=\"\${$_k:-}\""   # indirect lookup that works in bash 3.2 and zsh
    [ -n "$_cur" ] || export "$_k=$_v"
  done < "$_pc_cfg"
fi

# a PAPERCUT_LIB from the config file that no longer exists (moved or deleted checkout) is ignored
if [ -n "${PAPERCUT_LIB:-}" ] && [ ! -d "$PAPERCUT_LIB" ]; then unset PAPERCUT_LIB; fi
if [ -z "${PAPERCUT_LIB:-}" ] && [ -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" ]; then
  PAPERCUT_LIB="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
fi
export PAPERCUT_LIB
: "${PAPERCUT_PY:=python3}"; : "${QWEN_TTS_PY:=python3}"; : "${ASR_PY:=python3}"
export PAPERCUT_PY QWEN_TTS_PY ASR_PY

# papercut_config_set KEY VALUE: write or replace one line in the config file.
papercut_config_set() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$_pc_cfg")"; touch "$_pc_cfg"
  { grep -v "^$1=" "$_pc_cfg" || true; printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2"; } > "$_pc_cfg.tmp"
  mv "$_pc_cfg.tmp" "$_pc_cfg"
}

# papercut_find_chrome: print the Chrome or Chromium binary the audio render would use (same list as audio/render.mjs); fail if none.
papercut_find_chrome() {
  local p
  for p in "${CHROME_PATH:-}" "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" /Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium \
           /usr/bin/google-chrome /usr/bin/google-chrome-stable /usr/bin/chromium /usr/bin/chromium-browser; do
    if [ -n "$p" ] && [ -e "$p" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$p"; return 0; fi
  done
  return 1
}

namefframes-videodescriptionCreate, animate, review and render videos in code with fframes (Rust, SVG scenes, ffmpeg encoding, Skia GPU rendering). Use whenever the user wants a video, animation, motion graphic, explainer, promo, social clip, title card, podcast visual, lyric/caption video or any rendered .mp4/.webm made programmatically, or asks to change, fix, speed up or check an fframes video. Covers installing fframes, creating a project, designing good-looking motion, 3D shots (\`fframes::three\_d\`, three.js style scenes), sound (music, voice, SFX, loudness), watching it in a real-time preview window, and checking the result without watching it: frames and contact sheets as PNG, automatic problem detection, loudness numbers, fast draft and range renders.

# Making videos with fframes

[Permalink: Making videos with fframes](#making-videos-with-fframes)

[fframes](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes) is a Rust library that renders video from
code. A video is a Rust struct with a `render_frame(frame) -> Svgr` method: for every frame it
returns an SVG tree, built with the `svgr!` macro (SVG markup with `{rust expressions}`).
Scenes split the timeline, `timeline!` and springs animate values, an audio map places sound,
and ffmpeg encodes the result.

Each project gets a command line (from `fframes::cli`). Use it for everything: render a video,
open the real-time preview window, and look at frames, contact sheets and loudness numbers as
files you can read. Read `references/design.md` before designing, `references/api.md` while
writing code, `references/audio.md` for sound and `references/3d.md` for 3D shots
( `fframes::three_d`).

When matching a supplied video, first follow the reference-analysis guidance in
`references/design.md`. Its cuts, pacing and motion take precedence over the design defaults
below; fast edits and intentional black frames may be part of the requested result.

## Three rules before anything else

[Permalink: Three rules before anything else](#three-rules-before-anything-else)

### Plan before you write code

[Permalink: Plan before you write code](#plan-before-you-write-code)

Do not open the template and start animating. First:

1. Pin down the brief: who watches it and where (the platform decides format and length), the
one thing the viewer must remember, the tone, and the assets that exist (logo, product
shots, footage, music, voice-over). Ask the user for what is missing and matters. Never
invent product facts, numbers or quotes.
2. When the video is cut to music or a voice, choose the sound first. Its tempo, beats and
phrases set the timing of everything else.
3. Plan the motion design first, sync the motion design to the sound peaks to make a single
unique flow: where the elements will appear from, how they will transform. Try to create a
unique motion design for every scene so it looks unique and polished. The video shouldn't
look like a slide show.
4. Try to reason about the feeling for the person that is watching the final video and adjust
every piece of design you do accordingly: the flow, tempo, beats, motion, and colors.

### No slop

[Permalink: No slop](#no-slop)

Slop is a video made of default choices: it could be about any product with only the text
changed, and viewers recognise it within a second. Unless the user asks for it, do not ship:

- Template leftovers: the starter layout, colors, font or decorations, placeholder text, fake
logos, invented numbers.
- Beat spam: the whole frame zooming, shaking or flashing on every beat. Sync small things to
the beat (a stroke, a word, a spark) and change the whole frame only at a few cuts.
- One motion for everything: every element fading up 40 px with the same easing and duration.
- Static scenes: one thing appears, holds and fades while nothing else moves.
- Generic copy: "Introducing", "Unleash", "Seamless", "Next-level", three-word taglines
("Fast. Simple. Powerful."). Write on-screen text the way a person would say it.
- Text in general: the amount of text should be limited and on point.

Instead, give every element a reason tied to the subject and remove what has none. Spend the
effort on detail and motion rather than words: secondary motion, staggered entrances, drawn
strokes, objects that react to each other, elements carried across cuts. Before showing the
user anything, look at a strip and ask whether the video would still work for a different
product with only the text changed. If it would, change the idea, not the colors.

### The video is the Rust crate and `media/`

[Permalink: The video is the Rust crate and media/](#the-video-is-the-rust-crate-and-media)

The Rust crate and its media data define which part of a file plays, when and at what speed,
how a voice syncs with its picture, captions, music, grading and the export settings.
Keep reusable drawing behavior in Rust; timed caption text and per-word enum metadata can
live in VTT/JSON loaded through the same media provider. Put source files into `media/`
as the user gave them.

- Do not write Python, shell or ffmpeg scripts that cut, join, retime or grade media, that
generate Rust code or data tables, or that change the file after `$R render` (remux, retag,
replace the audio). Reading files to measure them ( `ffprobe`, a sync offset) is fine.
- Footage: make one scene for each spoken segment. `Clip::new("IMG_0926.mov", 19.2..24.7)`
plays seconds 19.2 to 24.7 of the file. The scene's `fn audio` places the voice recorded
with it, so picture and voice move together when an earlier scene changes. Inserts and
picture in picture are clips of the same scene ( `.at(1.2)`). `clip.image(&frame, ctx)` gives
an image: draw it with your own size, crop, transform, filter, mask or shader. To remove a
phrase, split the clip into two clips. See `references/api.md`.
- Write measured values (the offset between a camera file and an audio recorder) as named
constants with a comment that says what was measured and in which direction.
- If fframes cannot express something the user asked for, stop and tell the user what was
asked, which part fframes cannot do, and the closest result that works. Do not work around
it with an external tool.

## 1\. Install

[Permalink: 1. Install](#1-install)

Rust from [https://rustup.rs](https://rustup.rs), then the system libraries ffmpeg is built with:

```
# macOS
brew install pkg-config ffmpeg x264 x265 opus nasm ninja
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install -y yasm nasm ffmpeg libx264-dev libx265-dev libopus-dev libclang-dev clang ninja-build libvpx-dev libasound2-dev
# Arch
sudo pacman -S ninja yasm nasm ffmpeg x264 x265 opus clang
```

Windows links a prebuilt FFmpeg 9 shared build instead (set `FFMPEG_DIR` to the unzipped
`ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-gpl-shared` build from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, add its `bin` to `PATH`,
install LLVM with `winget install LLVM.LLVM` and set `LIBCLANG_PATH`). Details are in the
fframes README.

## 2\. Create a project

[Permalink: 2. Create a project](#2-create-a-project)

Update `cargo-fframes` before scaffolding each new video so it uses the latest published template.

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/main/scripts/new-video.sh | FFRAMES_REINSTALL=1 bash -s -- my-video --yes
```

Or use Cargo directly.

```
cargo install --locked cargo-fframes &&
  cargo fframes new my-video --format landscape --fps 30 --yes
```

Options: `--template single-scene|multi-scene`, `--format landscape|portrait|square|uhd`,
`--fps`, `--title`, `--backend`, `--dir`. The project depends on the fframes release that
matches the installed `cargo-fframes`; `--git` uses the repository's `main` branch instead. Always pass `--yes` so nothing waits for input.

Templates:

- `single-scene` (default): one scene. It adapts to every format; start here for single-shot
clips, title cards and portrait video.
- `multi-scene`: two scenes. Start here for anything with several scenes; it only accepts
`landscape` and `uhd`.

The template content is placeholder code that shows the API. Replace its layout, colors,
fonts and decorations with a design made for the video the user asked for.

**Use the Skia GPU backend (the default).** `cargo fframes new` picks Skia on Metal (macOS) or
Vulkan (Linux, Windows). It renders about 10x faster than the CPU backend and gives you the
real-time `preview` window. On macOS and Linux the first build downloads prebuilt Skia and ffmpeg
and only compiles the Rust dependencies (about a minute; other targets, or `metal` and `vulkan`
together, compile Skia from source for ~20 minutes). Start it right away and write the video
while it runs:

```
cd my-video && cargo build --release        # run in the background, the first build is the slow one
```

`--backend cpu` needs no Skia but has no preview window; pick it only when there is no GPU.

The project renders as generated:

```
my-video/
  src/lib.rs        # the video (from the template)
  src/main.rs       # the command line
  media/            # fonts, images and audio compiled into the binary (one starter font)
  README.md         # the commands below

```

Use `cargo run --release -- <command>` for CPU and GPU work, including frame checks.
The generated project already configures fast release rebuilds. For repeated commands, use
the shell function `F` (short for fframes).

```
F() { cargo run --release -- "$@"; }
```

Invoke the function as `F frame 2s`. In a workspace, select the video with `-p <package>`;
add `--bin <name>` if it has several binaries. After building an edit, reuse the binary in
`target/release/` for further checks or runtime argument changes. Run Cargo again after source
or embedded-media edits. Use only the requested checks for a narrow text/layout change;
broaden the review when timing, scenes or audio change.

To try title text in a generated project, run `./target/release/my-video frame 2s --title "Take two"`
with the project's binary name. Save the chosen title as the default in `src/main.rs` once.

## 3\. The loop

[Permalink: 3. The loop](#3-the-loop)

**Do not write tests at all when using this skill.** Do not create unit, integration,
snapshot or visual-regression tests, test modules, or test harnesses. Validate the video
with `inspect`, rendered frames, contact sheets, audio checks and the native preview.

**Preview, do not render.** If the video uses the GPU render backend and a GPU is available
on this machine, run the native preview (or show the user the command) instead of rendering
the video again after every change. Once the changes are ready to review:

1. Show a complete command in a copyable shell code block, using the actual project path and
package name; do not require the user to have defined the `F` helper. For example:
`cd /absolute/path/to/fframes && cargo run --release -p my-video -- preview 0s`.
2. Explicitly offer to run that preview for the user. If they have already authorized
opening or refreshing the preview, show the command and continue within that authorization.

After a requested change, set the command's start time to a specific second at or just before
the changed section, with enough lead-in to see its entrance or transition. For example,
`preview 8.5s` lets the user review a change around 9 seconds without replaying the beginning.
State which section they will see. Render the full video when the user requests the final
export; do not require another confirmation if that request is already explicit.

Choose checks that cover the change:

1. `F timeline` lists the scenes with their frame and second ranges, and every audio track.
Check structure and pacing here before looking at pixels.
2. `F inspect` checks a frame every 0.25 s plus the first and last frame of every scene. It
reports missing images, fonts or glyphs, text cut off by the edge of the canvas, invalid
SVG (zero-sized rectangles, bad radii), broken transforms and panics, each with its time
and scene. It exits with code 2 on errors. Fix everything it reports. A warning that only
appears on a scene's first frames is usually an entrance; check it with a strip.
3. `F strip <scene or range> -n 12` writes a contact sheet ( `strip.png`): evenly spaced frames
in one labelled image. Open it with your image tool. It is the fastest way to judge layout,
rhythm and motion. `F strip 2s,5s,9s` puts chosen times side by side.
4. `F frame Intro@end,Outro@50%` writes full-size PNGs into `frames/` for detail checks
(typography, alignment, contrast) and prints problems found in those frames. Judge small
details (contact between elements, edges, small shapes) on a sharp zoomed crop, never on a
scaled-down frame: `F frame 3s --crop 1100,520,240,120` (video pixels, zoomed to about
960 px wide). `--ids` outlines and names every element that has an `id`, to find which
shape is which.
5. `F onion "Intro@0..Intro@1s" -n 6` blends frames into one image ( `onion.png`) to show the
path and spacing of a movement: easing, overshoot, stagger.
6. `F preview Intro` opens a real-time window with sound for the user to watch (space
play/pause, h/l seek a second, j/k step a frame, q quit). It blocks until closed, so start
it in the background when running it for the user. Show the command and offer to launch
it as described above; after edits, use a specific second near the change.

When an encoded sample is needed, `F render Intro --draft` encodes one scene at half
resolution. `F render` writes the full video for a requested final export.

Before showing a finished video, run `F inspect --pops`: it renders every frame small and
warns about pops, parts of the picture that change in one frame between still frames, like an
element that appears, vanishes or jumps in front of another one instead of moving there. Each
warning gives the `frame ... --crop ...` command to look at it; repeats of the same region
(counters, blinking lights) are grouped into one warning.

Rules:

- Look at the PNGs before saying anything looks good.
- Prefer `strip` to many `frame` calls; add `--scale 0.5` when composition is all you need.
- Add `--json` when parsing output: the result goes to stdout, progress to stderr.
- Keep `--release`: debug builds render many times slower.

### Addressing time

[Permalink: Addressing time](#addressing-time)

`120` (frame), `3.2s`, `500ms`, `1:05.5`, `50%`, `start`, `end`; scenes by struct name, `Intro`
(also matches `IntroScene`, case-insensitive), `#3` (scene index), `Intro[1]` (second scene of
that type); inside a scene `Intro@1.2s`, `Intro@12`, `Intro@50%`, `Intro@end`. Ranges: `a..b`
(end exclusive), `a..`, `..b`, `all`, or a scene name for the whole scene. Separate several
times with commas.

### All commands

[Permalink: All commands](#all-commands)

commanduse it to`timeline`see scenes, durations, audio tracks and their mix settings`inspect [RANGE] [--every 0.1s | --all-frames] [--fail-on warning] [--pops]`find problems without rendering pixels; `--pops` also finds elements that pop in or out`strip [RANGE | TIMES] -n N [--columns 4] [--width 480] [--crop x,y,w,h]`review flow and motion in one image`frame TIMES [-o dir] [--svg] [--crop x,y,w,h] [--zoom N] [--ids]`full-size PNGs (and the laid-out SVG) of chosen frames, sharp crops, labelled elements`onion RANGE -n N`see a movement's trajectory and easing`svg TIME`read a frame's final SVG as text (positions, text, colors)`preview [TIME] [--paused] [--mute]`real-time window with sound, for the user`render [RANGE] [-o out.mp4] [--draft]`encode the video or a part of it (audio cut to match)`audio analyze [RANGE] [--waveform w.png]`loudness (LUFS), true peak, clipping, silence, per scene`audio at TIMES`which sounds play at a moment, where in their file and how loud`audio render [RANGE] -o a.wav`the mix as a WAV file

### Browser editor

[Permalink: Browser editor](#browser-editor)

fframes also has a web editor with a timeline and scrubbing, useful when a person wants to
tweak a video interactively. It runs the video compiled to WebAssembly and needs Node.js plus
`wasm-pack`; the setup is the `editor/` folder of the hello-world example in the fframes
repository ( [https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/hello-world](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/hello-world)).
Mention it when the user asks for a GUI editor. For watching use `preview`, and for your own
review use the CLI.

## 4\. Writing the video

[Permalink: 4. Writing the video](#4-writing-the-video)

```
impl Video for MyVideo<'_> {
    const FPS: usize = 30; const WIDTH: usize = 1920; const HEIGHT: usize = 1080;
    fn duration(&self) -> Duration<'_> { Duration::Auto }            // sum of the scenes
    fn audio(&self) -> AudioMap<'_> { AudioMap::none() }              // see references/audio.md
    fn define_scenes(&self) -> Scenes<'_> { Scenes::from(vec![&self.intro as &dyn Scene, &self.main]) }
    fn render_frame<'a>(&'a self, frame: Frame, ctx: &FFramesContext<'a, '_>) -> Svgr<'a> {
        fframes::svgr!(<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width={Self::WIDTH} height={Self::HEIGHT}>
            <rect width={Self::WIDTH} height={Self::HEIGHT} fill={BACKGROUND} />
            {ctx.render_scenes(&frame)}
        </svg>)
    }
}
```

- One scene per idea, 2-6 s each. Inside a scene `frame.seconds()` counts from the scene start.
- Default to `frame.animate(fframes::timeline!(...))` directly in `svgr!` attributes for
motion with fixed values. `svgr!` lifts these animations into cached statics. Define easings
inline in the timeline, including `Easing::Spring { mass: 1.0, stiffness: 180.0, damping: 20.0 }`;
named easing constants are optional. Leave the end time off a spring so it settles on its own.
- For dynamic values or calls outside that optimized pattern (including `animate_loop`),
construct timelines once on `self` and sample them by reference. Use cached
`AnimationRuntime` values for starts that change after construction or custom/subframe
clocks. Camera parameters and shader uniforms can use these APIs too; do not duplicate
springs or tween interpolation. See `references/design.md` and `references/api.md`.
- Markup without `{}` is cached across frames. Keep decoration literal and put animated values
on a wrapping `<g transform={..} opacity={..}>`.
- `render_frame` runs for every frame on several threads: no panics, file reads or heavy work
in it. Prepare data in the constructor or a `OnceLock`. Media lookups return `Option`; fall
back to `Svgr::empty()` instead of `expect`.
- Put every font file in `media/` and refer to it by family name, with a numeric
`font-weight`.
- Measure text rather than guess: `frame.text_width`, `frame.text_fit(.., TextOverflow::Ellipsis)`,
`frame.text_break_lines` for paragraphs. `inspect` catches text leaving the canvas, not text
leaving its own box, so check boxes in a `frame` PNG.
- For subtitles or timed lyrics, read `references/captions.md`: a VTT or JSON track in
`media/`, one `Captions` component kept on the video, `metadata.typed::<T>()` for
per-word effects. Never parse JSON or rebuild tracks per frame.
- Camera or phone footage plays through `fframes::Clip` inside scenes (see the rules at the
top). `frame.video_frame_at(ctx, file, seconds, None)` is one frame of a file (a freeze frame).
- GPU shaders (SkSL or Shadertoy GLSL) run on the Skia backend through `fframes::Shader`; they
take images and synced video frames as input (green-screen keying, color grading). See
`references/api.md`.
- 3D shots (products, devices, logos in a material, camera moves through a set) come from
`fframes::three_d` (feature `3d`), a three.js style scene graph that renders into an `<image>` with SVG below
and above it. Build the scene once, pose it per frame. See `references/3d.md`.

## 5\. Making it look good

[Permalink: 5. Making it look good](#5-making-it-look-good)

The short version of `references/design.md`:

- One idea per scene, large type, margins of 8-10% of the width, two or three colors plus
neutrals and one accent for emphasis.
- Elements enter with a spring or ease-out over 300-600 ms and leave faster, with ease-in over
200-300 ms. Related items stagger by 60-120 ms. Give the viewer 1-2 s to read after the
motion settles, and never move everything at once.
- Cross-fade scenes ( `fn overlap(&self) -> Overlap { Overlap::Previous(0.4) }`; the overlap
is added to the scene's `duration()`, see `references/api.md`) or carry an element across
the cut. Keep a little motion during holds so they do not look frozen.
- At 1920x1080: titles 96-140 px, body 44-60 px, at most about 8 words per line and 3 lines per
card. Portrait 1080x1920 is watched on a phone: same pixel sizes or larger, content inside
the middle 80% because platform UI covers the top and bottom.
- Check every scene against the checklist in `references/design.md` with a strip.

## 6\. Sound

[Permalink: 6. Sound](#6-sound)

Put audio files in `media/` (compiled in, mono unless `include_media_dir!(.., "media", stereo)`)
or load a folder at runtime with `MediaDirectory`, then place them:

```
AudioMap::from([
    AudioTrack::new("music.mp3", Second(0.)..Eof).gain_db(-18.).fade_in(1.).fade_out(2.).duck_under_voice(),
    AudioTrack::new("vo.wav", Second(0.6)..Eof).voice(),
    AudioTrack::new("whoosh.wav", Second(3.1)..Eof).gain_db(-8.),
])
```

Time sound effects from the same constants that drive the animation. Check levels with
`F audio analyze --waveform w.png` (about -14 LUFS integrated for web video, true peak below
-1 dBTP, no unintended silence) and `F audio at 3.1s` for what plays at an event. Then let
the user listen in `F preview`.

## 7\. Finish

[Permalink: 7. Finish](#7-finish)

1. `F inspect --fail-on warning` passes, or the remaining warnings are understood entrances.
2. A strip of every scene looks right and key frames are checked at full size.
3. Nothing from the "No slop" list at the top of this file is left in any strip.
4. `F audio analyze` shows sensible levels.
5. For GPU work awaiting review, show the preview command and offer to run it at the relevant
second. When the user requests the final export, run `F render -o out.mp4`, then confirm
size, frame count and audio with
`ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_type,width,height,nb_frames,duration out.mp4`.

For preview review, provide the concrete preview command, its start time and the offer to
launch it. After final export, provide the output path and duration.

## Troubleshooting

[Permalink: Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

- If a frame panics, rerun the failing command with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` and check the
first function of the video's source on the stack.

- Build fails in `ffmpeg-sys-fframes`: a system library from step 1 is missing ( `nasm`,
`pkg-config`, the codec `-dev` packages).

- Build fails in the Skia bindings ( `skia-bindings`) with bindgen or libclang errors (Skia
is only compiled from source when no prebuilt matches, e.g. `metal` and `vulkan` together): point `LIBCLANG_PATH` at a
working libclang (on macOS Xcode's:
`export LIBCLANG_PATH=$(xcode-select -p)/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/lib`).

- Skia bindings fail to compile on macOS 27 / Xcode 27 with ``cannot find type `_Traits` ``
in `std___hash_table___node_allocator`: only happens when Skia is compiled from source (the
prebuilt binaries ship their bindings). `skia-bindings` 0.153.3 lacks the bindgen rule
(rust-skia [#1335](https://github.com/rust-skia/rust-skia/pull/1335)); use one GPU backend so
the prebuilt download matches, or patch a copy of `skia-bindings-0.153.3` (add
`"std::__hash_table.*",` after `"std::__tree.*",` in `OPAQUE_TYPES` in
`build_support/skia_bindgen.rs`) through `[patch.crates-io]`.

- ``can't find crate for `fframes_media_dir_macro` `` on macOS 27 while the file exists: the
proc macro was linked by an older Rust whose output the macOS 27 loader rejects (a "LINKEDIT
string pool" error). Update Rust ( `rustup update`; 1.98 works) and rebuild.

- Text renders in the wrong font or not at all: `inspect` shows "No match for ... font-family";
add the font file to `media/` and use its exact family name.

# Papercut kit catalog (generated by tools/catalog.py; do not edit)

The kit is synced into each project at `src/lib/` (`papercut/sync_kit.sh`). Scenes import it as `../lib/<file>`.
Read this file instead of the kit source. Open a source file only when you need a detail that isn't here.
If a scene needs something the kit lacks, build it in your scene file. The lead promotes reusable pieces into the kit after the episode (HARVEST.md).

## `cast/Critter.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/cast/Critter'`)

> The one base creature for the whole cast: a boxy paper critter with eyes only and stubby limbs. Cast members differ by colour, accessory and name pill. (x, y) is the ground point under the body.

- `type Expr = 'idle' | 'sleep' | 'shock' | 'happy' | 'worried' | 'blink' | 'squint';`
- `type Acc = 'none' | 'postCap' | 'monocle' | 'headphones' | 'visor' | 'cap' | 'hardhat' | 'beret' | 'glasses' | 'headset' | 'bowtie';`
- `<Critter x: number; y: number; size?: number; color?: string; shade?: string; expr?: Expr; acc?: Acc; tag?: string; tagColor?: string; armR?: number; armRAngle?: number; armL?: number; armLAngle?: number; // reach 0–1, angle deg (negative = up) lean?: number; lift?: n…>`

## `fonts.ts`  (import from `'../lib/fonts'`)

> Fonts from local files in public/fonts/: the exact woff2 files @remotion/google-fonts used to fetch at render time. Two problems this fixes: 1. Network: every render tab fetched the fonts from fonts.gstatic.com, so a Wi-Fi blip failed the whole render. 2. Banner jitter: TapeBanner sizes its text with fitText(). A tab that measured before the font arrived cached the fallback width, so the banner ju

- `const fontsReady: Promise<void> = Promise.all(`
- `const fontsLoaded = () => loaded;`

## `paper/backdrops.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/backdrops'`)

> Backdrops: 24 paper-diorama sets (1080x1920 JPEGs in public/bg/backdrops/) to use instead of <Room>, so each scene can sit in its own place. Layout contract for every set: floor line near y 1420 (measured per set in BACKDROPS), calm middle band for props and UI, calm top for the banner, plain bottom for captions, light from the top-left, no people or text baked in. Stand props and critters on BACK

- `const BACKDROPS = {`: Every backdrop name with its measured floor line (px y at 1080x1920) and mood (day, night, warm, cool). Props and critters stand on floorY.
- `type BackdropName = keyof typeof BACKDROPS;`: Union of the backdrop names, for typing a scene's `backdrop` prop.
- `<Backdrop name: BackdropName; tint?: string; dim?: number>`: Backdrop: full-frame generated set (object-fit cover), a drop-in for <Room>. Optional `tint` multiplies a colour over it, `dim` (0-1) darkens it toward black.

## `paper/camera.tsx`  (import from `'../lib/paper/camera'`)

> Camera moves for papercut sets: parallax orbit (OrbitCamera + Depth layers), foreground pass, rack focus, snap zoom, pull-back reveal and freeze frame. A fake camera moving through a paper diorama; all motion from useCurrentFrame(). Moves transform the whole frame, so the banner zone (y < 420) and the caption band (y 1420-1580) move too: keep key props and faces out of both.

- `<OrbitCamera dur: number; yaw?: number; drift?: [number, number]; push?: number; focus?: number; depth?: number; origin?: [number, number]; children: React.ReactNode>`: Parallax orbit: the camera arcs `yaw` degrees (16) around the focal plane while dollying to `push`, so <Depth z> layers separate. `origin` = pivot px (near the floor line), `depth` = layer spacing, `drift` = pan px.
- `<Depth z: number; cover?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Depth layer in <OrbitCamera>: z 0 = backdrop (auto-oversized to cover), ~0.5 = props and cast, 1 = foreground. Lay each out at normal screen positions; the camera adds the parallax. Outside an OrbitCamera it is a plain fill.
- `<ForegroundPass at: number; dur?: number; kind?: 'leaf' | 'cable' | 'block'; from?: 'left' | 'right'; y?: number; blur?: number; scale?: number; dim?: number>`: Blurred paper object (kind leaf | cable | block) sweeps across the lens from the `from` side over `dur` frames from `at`, and a faint shadow dims the set. Put it last in the stack; `y` moves its anchor.
- `<RackFocus from?: number; to?: number; at?: number; dur?: number; bleed?: boolean; returnAt?: number; holdFrames?: number; children: React.ReactNode>`: Blur wrapper: eases blur `from` to `to` px over `dur` frames from `at`. Wrap the backdrop (set `bleed` to hide its soft edge) or a hero prop; use opposite pairs on two planes to pull focus between them. `returnAt` / `holdFrames` make it a …
- `<SnapZoom at: number; x?: number; y?: number; to?: number; settle?: number; shake?: number; roll?: number; blur?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Punch-in to the focal point (x, y): 1 to `to` (1.25) in 4 frames with radial motion blur, a 3-frame shake and a little roll, then settles at `settle`. For numbers and joke landings: `at` = the frame the thing lands.
- `<PullBack dur: number; x: number; y: number; from?: number; at?: number; blur?: boolean; children: React.ReactNode>`: Pull-back reveal: starts `from`x (2.8) tight on the detail at (x, y), eases out to the whole set over `dur` frames with motion blur on the first frames. Edges stay covered. Shows scale.
- `<FreezeFrame at: number; label?: string; x?: number; y?: number; rot?: number; size?: number; mark?: 'left' | 'right' | false; children: React.ReactNode>`: Meme beat: holds the child on frame `at` (Freeze), desaturates, darkens the edges, then slaps on a torn paper `label` (at x, y) with a stamp bounce and a record-scratch mark (left|right). Pair with SFX `scratch` at `at`.

339 api.md
# fframes API cheat sheet

For VTT/JSON subtitles, typed word metadata, reusable highlights and caching, see
[captions.md](captions.md). The `captions` feature adds SVG rendering; subtitle parsing
and media loading remain available without it.

Examples in the fframes repository worth reading: [beta](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/beta) (scenes, images), [audio-announce](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/audio-announce)
(audio visualisation, video sources), [teej-podcast](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/teej-podcast) (Skia backend, stereo
media loaded at runtime), [shaders](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/shaders) and [neon-triangle](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/tree/main/examples/neon-triangle) (GPU
shaders).

## svgr!

SVG markup with Rust in braces. Attributes and text children take strings, numbers, `Color`,
`Transform`, another `Svgr`, or a `Vec<Svgr>` / iterator collected to a `Vec`.

```rust
fframes::svgr!(
    <g transform={Transform::translate(x, y)} opacity={opacity}>
        // comments are `//` lines
        <rect x="0" y="0" width={w} height="80" rx="16" fill={ACCENT} />
        <text x="24" y="54" font-family="Inter" font-size="40" font-weight="600" fill="#fff">
            "Label: " {value.to_string()}
        </text>
        {items}   // Vec<Svgr>
    </g>
)
```

- Literal text children are quoted strings. `Svgr::empty()` renders nothing.
- Subtrees without `{}` are hashed at compile time and cached by the renderers: keep static
  decoration static, wrap animated values around it.
- Gradients, clip paths, masks, filters go into `<defs>` like normal SVG and are referenced
  with `url(#id)`. Give ids unique names per component instance if repeated.
- Images: `href={self.media.logo_png.href()}` (field named after the file in `media/`) or
  `ctx.get_image("logo.png").map(|i| i.href())`.

## Video and Scene

```rust
impl Video for MyVideo<'_> {
    const FPS: usize = 30;
    const WIDTH: usize = 1920;
    const HEIGHT: usize = 1080;
    const BACKGROUND_COLOR: Color = Color::BLACK;   // painted under every frame
    fn duration(&self) -> Duration<'_>;             // Seconds(f32), Frames(usize), FromAudio("f"), FromVideo("f"), Auto, a + b
    fn audio(&self) -> AudioMap<'_>;                // AudioMap::none() or tracks
    fn define_scenes(&self) -> Scenes<'_>;          // optional
    fn render_frame<'a>(&'a self, frame: Frame, ctx: &FFramesContext<'a, '_>) -> Svgr<'a>;
}

impl Scene for Intro<'_> {
    fn duration(&self) -> Duration<'_>;
    fn render_frame<'a>(&'a self, frame: Frame, ctx: &FFramesContext<'a, '_>) -> Svgr<'a>;
    fn overlap(&self) -> Overlap { Overlap::Previous(0.4) }  // optional cross-fade window
    fn audio(&self) -> AudioMap<'_> { .. }                   // optional, relative to the scene
}
```

- Scenes must be zero sized or fields of the video (`&self.intro`). Scene names in the CLI
  are the struct names (`Intro`, `IntroScene` both match `IntroScene`). Override
  `fn name(&self) -> &'static str` to name scenes yourself, e.g. one `Shot { kind }` struct
  used for every scene and still addressed as `Smooch@2s` in the CLI.
- `Overlap` is added on top of `duration()`: with `Overlap::Previous(0.5)` the scene starts
  0.5 s before the previous one ends and runs `duration() + 0.5` s. To land scene `i` on a cue
  (a lyric, a beat) after a 0.5 s transition, use `duration = cue[i + 1] - cue[i]` and
  `Overlap::Previous(0.5)`; the scene then covers `cue[i] - 0.5 .. cue[i + 1]`. Check with
  `timeline`.
- `ctx.render_scenes(&frame)` in the video's `render_frame` renders the active scene(s).
- `frame.index` / `frame.seconds()` are scene relative inside a scene; `frame.global_index`
  is the video frame. `ctx.get_scene_info(&self.intro)` gives a scene's resolved range.
- `ctx.current_video_size` is the output size (scaled by `--scale`); trees drawn at
  `WIDTH`x`HEIGHT` are scaled automatically.

## Animation

For motion with fixed values, put `frame.animate(fframes::timeline!(...))` directly in the
`svgr!` attribute. The SVG macro lifts the timeline into a `lazy_static` animation, resolving
its easing runtimes once. It is fine to define the easing directly in the `timeline!` block;
named constants are optional.

```rust
use fframes::{Color, Transform, animation::Easing};

// keyframes: at START [=> END | , duration D], animate FROM => TO, EASING
fframes::svgr!(
    <g opacity={frame.animate(fframes::timeline!(
        at 0.0 => 0.3, animate 0.0 => 1.0, Easing::EaseOut,
    ))}
    transform={frame.animate(fframes::timeline!(
        at 0.0, animate Transform::translate(0, 60) => Transform::translate(0, 0),
            Easing::Spring { mass: 1.0, stiffness: 180.0, damping: 20.0 },
        at 2.5 => 2.8, animate Transform::translate(0, 0) => Transform::translate(0, -40),
            Easing::EaseIn,
    ))}>
        <rect x="160" y="240" width="600" height="120" rx="24"
            fill={frame.animate(fframes::timeline!(
                at 0.0 => 1.0, animate Color::hex("#fff") => Color::hex("#0ea5e9"),
                    Easing::EaseInOut,
            ))}
        />
    </g>
)
```

- The optimizer recognizes an attribute block whose sole expression is
  `frame.animate(timeline!(...))` (also with `&timeline!(...)`). Use `f32` literals or
  imported `Color` / `Transform` constructors for the animated values; the cached timeline
  cannot capture locals such as `self`, a loop index, or a runtime start time.
- This caching belongs to `svgr!`, not `timeline!` alone. Calls outside the macro, nested
  inside other expressions, and `animate_loop` do not use this optimization. For those,
  initialize `KeyFramesAnimation` fields once in the constructor and sample with
  `frame.animate(&self.animation)` / `frame.animate_loop(&self.animation)`. Data-dependent
  staggering can also build one timeline per item in the constructor. Camera parameters,
  shader uniforms and custom projection can consume these cached animations.
- Before the first keyframe the value is `from`, after the last it stays at `to`.
- Stored timelines also support `f64` and other types implementing `Animatable` with the
  required bounds; the inline optimizer supports the built-in forms listed above.
- When a start time changes after construction, use `frame.animate_runtime(AnimateRuntimeInput {
  on_second, from, to, animation_runtime: &self.runtime })`, with `self.runtime` initialized
