on_second, from, to, animation_runtime: &self.runtime })`, with `self.runtime` initialized
  once using `AnimationRuntime::new(duration, &easing)`. Known item offsets belong in cached
  `timeline!` values, not per-frame runtime construction. For springs, an explicit duration
  caps the natural settle time; omit the end in `timeline!` to let the spring settle.
- For precomputed geometry, motion-blur subframes or a custom clock,
  `runtime.solve(&elapsed_seconds)` evaluates the same easing
  directly. Handle times before the start and after `get_duration()` explicitly: `solve`
  does not clamp them. Use a custom curve only when the required motion is not represented
  by the available easings.
- Easing: `Linear`, `EaseIn`, `EaseOut`, `EaseInOut`, `CubicBezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, `Spring {..}`.
  Use the named ones and `Spring`; `design.md` says which fits where.
- `Transform { translate_x, translate_y, scale: Scale { x, y }, rotate, .. }`,
  `Transform::translate(x, y)`. Scale around a point by translating by `p * (1 - s)`.

### Matching a fractional-rate reference

`Video::FPS` is currently an integer. A 30000/1001 fps source played at 30 fps has different
timing even when every frame is retained. Keep edit boundaries as integer source frames;
for source-time effects, compute `source_frame * fps_den / fps_num` and sample an easing
runtime or bind a custom shader clock. Ordinary `frame.animate` follows the frame's integer
fps; placing keyframes at `source_frame / Video::FPS` preserves their frame positions.

When exact source timing is required, retime the final export and verify every frame is
retained. For the specific 30000/1001 case, FFmpeg video options
`-vf 'settb=1/30000,setpts=N*1001' -r 30000/1001 -fps_mode cfr -video_track_timescale 30000`
give a 1001-tick frame interval. Do not combine output `-r` with `-fps_mode passthrough`.
This export step does not change the native preview's clock. See `audio.md` for preserving
the original soundtrack during muxing.

## Text

```rust
use fframes::{BreakLinesOpts, FontQuery, TextAlign, TextOverflow};
let font = FontQuery { family: "Inter", size: 48, weight: 500, ..Default::default() };
let w: Option<usize> = frame.text_width(ctx, font, "Title");
// text_fit returns Option<Cow<str>>; svgr! needs a String or &str, so convert it
let fitted: String = frame
    .text_fit(ctx, font, long_title, 900, TextOverflow::Ellipsis)
    .map(|text| text.into_owned())
    .unwrap_or_else(|| long_title.to_owned());
// text_break_lines returns Option<Svgr>: a ready <text> with one <tspan> per line
let paragraph: Svgr = frame
    .text_break_lines(ctx, text, BreakLinesOpts {
        font, width: 900, x: 160, y: 400, align: TextAlign::Left, fill: "#0f172a", ..Default::default()
    })
    .unwrap_or_default();
```

The helpers take `&mut frame` and return `None` when the font is not loaded; use the same
family, size and weight in the `<text>` attributes. `text-anchor="middle"` centers on `x`.

## Media

- `include_media_dir!(pub struct MyMedia, "media")` embeds a folder; the path is relative to
  the Cargo workspace root, which in a generated project is the project folder. Call
  `MyMedia::prepare()` in `main.rs`. Fonts register by family name, audio decodes to mono;
  `include_media_dir!(pub struct MyMedia, "media", stereo)` keeps stereo files stereo.
- Large or stereo files: `let dir = MediaDirectory::read_folder("assets")?; let media = dir.process_media_source()?;`
  and combine providers with `CombinedMediaProvider::from([&static_media as &dyn MediaProvider, &media])`.
- Video frames: `frame.get_synced_video_frame(ctx, "clip.mp4", &SyncVideoFrameInput { start_from, looping, speed, editor_fallback_image })`
  (`speed: 2.0` plays twice as fast, `..Default::default()` keeps 1.0)
  then `<image href={video_frame.href()} .../>` (needs the `compile-time-svgtree` feature).
  `start_from` is when the video starts on the timeline, not a position in the file.
- Footage: `Clip::new("IMG_0926.mov", 19.2..24.7)` is seconds 19.2 to 24.7 of the file,
  `Clip::new("cam.mp4", 0.0..)` the whole file (`.at(1.2)` starts it at 1.2 s of the scene, `.speed(1.5)`, `.reverse()`, `.looping()`).
  In a scene, `fn duration` returns `self.face.duration()` and `render_frame` takes
  `self.face.image(&frame, ctx)` (or `image_at_width(&frame, ctx, 440)` for a small picture in
  picture), an `Option<ImageData>` drawn as `<image href={image.href()} ...>` with any
  transform, filter, mask or shader. `{option_of_svgr}` in `svgr!` draws nothing for `None`.
  Put the voice of the clip into the scene's `audio` with `.offset(...)` into the audio file,
  so it moves with the scene. Cut a phrase by splitting the clip into two clips, never by
  cutting the file.
- One frame of a file: `frame.video_frame_at(ctx, "IMG_0926.mov", 21.0, None)` (seconds of the file).
- Subtitles: `ctx.get_subtitles("subs.vtt").and_then(|s| frame.get_subtitle_phrase(s))`.
- Audio spectrum: `frame.visualize_audio_frame(VisualizeFrameInput { audio, sample_size: SampleSize::S256, smooth_level: 4, window: Some(WindowFunction::Hann) })`.

## Lottie animations

To play a Lottie `.json` file, enable the `lottie` feature
(`fframes = { features = ["lottie"] }`) and put the file into the media folder, like an image.

```rust
use fframes::LottieOptions;

let confetti = frame.play_lottie(ctx, "confetti.json", LottieOptions {
    start: 1.5,          // second of the video or scene, nothing is drawn before it
    looping: true,       // without it the last frame stays
    x: 660.0,
    y: 240.0,
    width: Some(600.0),  // the height follows; give both to fit the file into a box
    ..Default::default()
});
fframes::svgr!(<svg ...>{confetti}</svg>)
```

`media.confetti_json.duration()` (a field of the `include_media_dir!` struct) gives the length
for `Video::duration`. Text layers, image layers, time remapping, blend modes and effects are
not drawn.

## GPU shaders (Skia backend)

`fframes::Shader` runs SkSL, or pasted Shadertoy GLSL, on the Skia GPU surface while the frame
is drawn. SVG transforms, clips, masks and opacity apply to the layer like to any element.

```rust
use fframes::{Shader, ShaderUniforms};

// once, in the constructor (the renderer compiles and caches it)
let aurora = Shader::sksl(include_str!("shaders/aurora.sksl"));   // half4 main(float2 coord)
let torus = Shader::shadertoy(include_str!("shaders/torus.glsl")); // void mainImage(out vec4, in vec2)

// in render_frame
let layer = self.aurora.draw(&frame, ShaderUniforms::new()
    .float("uSpeed", 0.6)
    .color("uTint", frame.animate(&tint)));
fframes::svgr!(<image href={layer.href()} x="0" y="0" width="1920" height="1080" />)
```

- Built-in uniforms when declared: `iResolution` (the `<image>` size), `iTime`, `iTimeDelta`,
  `iFrame`. Pass images with `.image("iChannel0", photo)` where `photo` comes from

# Sound for fframes videos

You cannot hear the result. Place sound from the timeline, check it with the numbers below,
and ask the user to listen in `cargo run --release -- preview`.

## Files

- Short SFX and music can live in `media/` (embedded, decoded at compile time; mp3, wav, flac,
  aac, ogg, m4a). Embedded audio is mono unless the macro gets the `stereo` option:
  `include_media_dir!(pub struct Media, "media", stereo)` keeps both channels (twice the size).
- Stereo music, voice-overs and anything large: a folder loaded at runtime keeps stereo:

```rust
let audio_dir = fframes::MediaDirectory::read_folder("audio")?;
let audio = audio_dir.process_media_source()?;
let media = fframes::CombinedMediaProvider::from([&static_media as &dyn fframes::MediaProvider, &audio]);
// RenderOptions { media: Some(&media), .. }
```

- Generating placeholder sounds without assets: `sox` (`sox -n pop.wav synth 0.08 sine 880 fade 0 0.08 0.07`)
  or `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:duration=0.2" tick.wav`. Tell the user they are
  placeholders.

## Placing tracks

```rust
use fframes::{AudioMap, AudioTrack, AudioTimestamp::*, Ducking, FadeCurve};

fn audio(&self) -> AudioMap<'_> {
    AudioMap::from([
        AudioTrack::new("music.mp3", Second(0.)..Eof).gain_db(-18.).fade_in(1.5).fade_out(2.5)
            .fade_curve(FadeCurve::EqualPower).duck_under_voice(),
        AudioTrack::new("vo_01.wav", Second(0.6)..Eof).voice(),
        AudioTrack::new("vo_02.wav", Second(6.2)..Eof).voice(),
        AudioTrack::new("whoosh.wav", Second(TRANSITION_AT - 0.15)..Eof).gain_db(-10.),
        AudioTrack::new("pop.wav", Second(ITEM_AT + 0.05)..Eof).gain_db(-12.).pan(0.3),
        AudioTrack::new("take.wav", Second(20.)..Second(24.)).offset(3.2),  // file 3.2s..7.2s
    ])
}
```

- Timestamps: `Second(f32)` (sample accurate), `Frame(n)`, `Time { minutes, seconds }`,
  `Eof` as the end (= play to the end of the file), `DurationOfAudio("f")`, and `+`/`-`.
- Scenes can have their own `fn audio` with times relative to the scene start: sounds move
  with the scene when durations change.
- Derive SFX times from the same constants that drive the animation. Whooshes start ~150 ms
  before the movement peak; pops/clicks land on the frame the element appears (+0-50 ms).
- Gain guidelines relative to a normalised voice at 0 dB: music under voice -16 to -22 dB
  (plus ducking), music alone -8 to -12 dB, UI SFX -8 to -14 dB, whooshes -8 to -12 dB.
- `duck_under_voice()` = -12 dB, 0.2 s attack before the voice, 0.3 s hold, 0.8 s release,
  voice gaps under 0.8 s merged. `.duck(Ducking { depth_db: -15., ..Default::default() })` to tune.
- The master bus sums linearly and limits peaks at -1 dBFS (`RenderOptions::audio_mix`), so
  loud overlaps do not distort, but a limiter working hard squashes the mix: fix gains rather
  than relying on it.

## Checking without listening

```bash
F timeline                         # every track with its seconds, gain, fades, voice/ducked
F audio at 3.1s,6.2s               # what plays at an event, position in the file, level, ducking
F audio analyze                    # loudness report, per scene
F audio analyze --waveform w.png   # read the image: waveform, loudness curve, scene lines, cue ticks
F audio render Intro -o intro.wav  # the mix of one scene, if the user wants to listen
```

Targets for the report:
- Integrated loudness: about -14 LUFS for web/social (-16 for podcasts, -23 for broadcast).
  More than 2 LU off: adjust gains (all tracks) or `audio_mix.master_gain_db`.
- True peak at or below -1 dBTP; `clipped_samples` 0.
- Loudness range 4-10 LU for music videos and explainers; far higher means quiet and loud
  parts need balancing.
- `silent_ranges` only where silence is intended (an unexpected one means a track ends early
  or a file is missing: check `missing_files` and `timeline`).
- Per scene: scenes with voice should be within ~2 LU of each other.

The waveform image shows cue ticks (yellow) under the scene lines (purple): each sound should
sit where its visual event is. For a precise check use `audio at` on the event time and a
`frame` of the same time.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fast cached render for papercut Remotion projects (and dialogue projects, see below). render.sh calls this.

  python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/render.py [--workers 3] [--conc 4] [--force] [--keep]     (run from the Remotion project dir)
  -> out/<episode.json "out">.mp4, plus decode-error count, stream info and loudness.
  env: PAPERCUT_PY  python with numpy + soundfile, used for the audio mix (tools/mix.py). Default python3.
  Needs node/npx (Remotion), ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH.

What makes it faster than three fresh `remotion render` chunks:
  1. Bundle once. `remotion bundle` runs only when a source file changed; every segment renders from that bundle.
  2. One segment per scene, cached. A segment's key hashes the shared files (everything except scene-owned files:
     kit, plan.json, captions, banners, public images, package-lock) plus the files its scene imports from
     src/scenes/ (S06ShowWork.tsx, S06ShowWork.parts.tsx, a shared Tape.parts.tsx...). After a fix to
     one scene, only that scene re-renders; a VO/plan/kit change re-renders everything. Audio isn't in any key.
  3. ProRes HQ intermediates (all-intra, cheap to encode, so Chrome gets the CPU), joined with the concat demuxer
     and encoded to H.264 once. The old path encoded x264 twice (chunks and final).
  4. Audio mix + loudnorm runs in parallel with the video render.
Frames are captured as JPEG q95 (Remotion's default is q80): +2.4 dB PSNR on the intermediate for ~8% more capture time.
Colour: Remotion tags ProRes bt470bg but encodes with the BT.709 matrix in limited range; checked against a
`remotion still` PNG (BT.709 in = 36.3 dB, BT.601 in = 33.3 dB after the final encode).
Dialogue projects (src/timeline.json from dialogue_timeline.py, no scenes) render as three equal segments keyed on all sources.
No template for them ships with the library; the branch is kept for projects that bring their own.
"""

def sha(*parts):
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    for p in parts:
        h.update(p if isinstance(p, bytes) else str(p).encode())
        h.update(b'\0')
    return h.hexdigest()


def file_sha(path, memo={}):
    if path not in memo:
        with open(path, 'rb') as f:
            memo[path] = hashlib.sha1(f.read()).hexdigest()
    return memo[path]

# Butt the final narration lines together, write word captions and the scene plan. Config: episode.json
#   {"narration": "../narration", "timing": "timing_narrator.js", "fps": 30, "start": 0.2, "gap": 0.22, "hold": 2.3,
#    "scenes": [["S01Hook", "l1_hook", 0], ["S02Yes", "l1_hook", "and"], ...]}   (first word: index or exact word)
#    "hook": {...}   (optional, see below)
#   out: public/vo/voiceover.wav, public/vo/captions.json (Remotion Caption[]), src/plan.json
#   usage (from the Remotion project dir): python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/build_vo.py
import json, os, subprocess, wave
EP = json.load(open("episode.json"))
SRC = EP.get("narration", "../narration")
FPS, START, GAP, HOLD = EP.get("fps", 30), EP.get("start", 0.2), EP.get("gap", 0.22), EP.get("hold", 2.3)
VO = json.loads(open(f"{SRC}/" + os.environ.get("VO_TIMING", EP.get("timing", "timing_narrator.js"))).read().split("const VO = ", 1)[1].rstrip().rstrip(";"))
SCENES = [tuple(s) for s in EP["scenes"]]
GAPS = EP.get("gaps", {})

words, t, parts, line_at = [], START, [], {}
for lid in VO["order"]:
    seg = VO["seg"][lid]
    w = wave.open(f"{SRC}/{seg['file']}"); dur = w.getnframes() / w.getframerate()
    line_at[lid] = (t, len(words))
    for x in seg["words"]:
        words.append({"text": x["w"], "startMs": round((t + x["s"]) * 1000), "endMs": round((t + x["e"]) * 1000), "line": lid})
    parts.append((seg["file"], t)); t += dur + GAP + GAPS.get(lid, 0)   # "gaps": {"l7_setup": 0.3} = an extra beat after a line
total = t - GAP + HOLD

os.makedirs("public/vo", exist_ok=True)
inp, flt = [], []
for k, (f, at) in enumerate(parts):
    inp += ["-i", f"{SRC}/{f}"]; ms = int(round(at * 1000))
    flt.append(f"[{k}:a]aresample=48000,adelay={ms}[a{k}]")
flt.append("".join(f"[a{k}]" for k in range(len(parts))) + f"amix=inputs={len(parts)}:normalize=0,apad,atrim=0:{total:.3f}[o]")
subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", *inp, "-filter_complex", ";".join(flt), "-map", "[o]", "-ac", "1", "public/vo/voiceover.wav"], check=True)
# silent music/fx placeholders until audio/render.mjs writes the real ones, so scene agents' qa.sh renders work
os.makedirs("public/audio", exist_ok=True)
for a in ("music", "fx"):
    if not os.path.exists(f"public/audio/{a}.wav"):
        subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo", "-t", f"{total:.3f}", f"public/audio/{a}.wav"], check=True)

caps = [{"text": (" " if i else "") + w["text"], "startMs": w["startMs"], "endMs": w["endMs"], "timestampMs": (w["startMs"] + w["endMs"]) // 2, "confidence": 1}
        for i, w in enumerate(words)]
json.dump(caps, open("public/vo/captions.json", "w"))

starts = []
for sid, lid, first in SCENES:
    base = line_at[lid][1]; lw = [w for w in words if w["line"] == lid]
    idx = first if isinstance(first, int) else next(i for i, w in enumerate(lw) if w["text"] == first)
    starts.append(base + idx)
cut = [0] + [round((words[i]["startMs"] / 1000 - 0.08) * FPS) for i in starts[1:]] + [round(total * FPS)]
plan = {"fps": FPS, "durationInFrames": cut[-1], "scenes": []}
for k, (sid, lid, _) in enumerate(SCENES):
    a, b = cut[k], cut[k + 1]
    ws = [{"text": w["text"], "f": round(w["startMs"] / 1000 * FPS) - a, "e": round(w["endMs"] / 1000 * FPS) - a}
          for w in words if a <= round(w["startMs"] / 1000 * FPS) < b]
    plan["scenes"].append({"id": sid, "from": a, "durationInFrames": b - a, "words": ws})
# Optional hook title (the cover text on screen from frame 0; see kit/paper/hook.tsx):
#   "hook": {"lines": [["AI", "LEAKED"], ["13,000+"]], "hot": ["13,000+"], "until": "yes" | ["yes", 2], "size": 108, "top": 220}
#   It leaves at the onset of the `until` word (its n-th occurrence), or after "hold" seconds (default 2.4).
H = EP.get("hook")
if H:
    if "until" in H:
        uw, un = (H["until"], 1) if isinstance(H["until"], str) else H["until"]
        hits = [w for w in words if w["text"].strip(".,!?;:'\"").lower() == uw.lower()]
        out = round(hits[un - 1]["startMs"] / 1000 * FPS)
    else:
        out = round(H.get("hold", 2.4) * FPS)
    plan["hook"] = {**{k: v for k, v in H.items() if k not in ("until", "hold")}, "outAt": out}
    print(f"hook title until frame {out} ({out / FPS:.2f}s)")
json.dump(plan, open("src/plan.json", "w"), indent=1)
for s in plan["scenes"]:
    flag = "  <-- under 1.2 s: merge it into a neighbour" if s["durationInFrames"] < 36 else ""
    print(f"{s['id']:16s} {s['from']/FPS:6.2f}s  {s['durationInFrames']/FPS:4.2f}s  " + " ".join(f"{w['text']}@{w['f']}" for w in s["words"]) + flag)
print("total", round(total, 2), "s", cut[-1], "frames")

# SFX cue sheet → tools/cues.json for audio/render.mjs.   usage (from the papercut project dir): python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/cues.py
#   in : src/plan.json, tools/cue_sheet.json + tools/cue_sheet.d/*.json {"S01Hook": [["Ask", 0, "hit", -6], ...]}  (word prefix, nth match, sfx, offset frames)
#        episode.json "whipScene" (the scene that gets a whip instead of a cut), "cutSfx" (per-scene cut sound), "noAir", optional "outroLead" frames (default 40)
#   SFX names must exist in audio/sfx (see audio/CATALOG.md).
#   optional episode.json "sfxMinGapMs" (default 0 = off): drop a decorative cue (sparkle, pop, pop3, boing, toss, slide, tick)
#   when another cue already sits within that many ms before or after it, so layered hits don't pile up.
import json, re, os, sys
plan = json.load(open("src/plan.json")); FPS = plan["fps"]
EP = json.load(open("episode.json")) if os.path.exists("episode.json") else {}
SHEET = json.load(open("tools/cue_sheet.json")) if os.path.exists("tools/cue_sheet.json") else {}
# scene agents write their own rows to tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json (no write conflicts); those override the main sheet
import glob
for q in sorted(glob.glob("tools/cue_sheet.d/*.json")): SHEET.update(json.load(open(q)))
LIB = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "audio", "sfx")
norm = lambda w: re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", w.lower())
cues, bad = [], []
# optional episode.json "cutSfx": the sound on each scene start, {"*": default, "<Scene>": name}; "" = silent. Without it every
# cut gets "cut" (a soft swish) and whipScene gets "whip". Match the transition: tearAway "rip", tapePull "tape-peel", keyhole "click".
CUTSFX = EP.get("cutSfx", {})
for s in plan["scenes"]:
    if s["from"] > 0:
        cut = CUTSFX.get(s["id"], "whip" if s["id"] == EP.get("whipScene") else CUTSFX.get("*", "cut"))
        if cut: cues.append({"t": round(s["from"] / FPS, 3), "type": cut})
    for word, n, typ, off in SHEET.get(s["id"], []):
        hits = [w for w in s["words"] if norm(w["text"]).startswith(norm(word))]
        if len(hits) <= n: bad.append(f"{s['id']}: no word '{word}'#{n}"); continue
        if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(LIB, f"{typ}.js")): bad.append(f"{s['id']}: unknown sfx '{typ}'")
        cues.append({"t": round((s["from"] + hits[n]["f"] + off) / FPS, 3), "type": typ})
last = plan["scenes"][-1]
cues.append({"t": round((last["from"] + last["durationInFrames"] - EP.get("outroLead", 40)) / FPS, 3), "type": "outro"})
cues.sort(key=lambda c: c["t"])
gap = EP.get("sfxMinGapMs", 0) / 1000
if gap:
    DECOR = {"sparkle", "pop", "pop3", "boing", "toss", "slide", "tick"}
    keep = [c for c in cues if c["type"] not in DECOR]          # main hits, cuts, whips, outro always stay
    for c in (c for c in cues if c["type"] in DECOR):
        if all(abs(c["t"] - k["t"]) >= gap for k in keep): keep.append(c)
    print(f"declutter ({EP['sfxMinGapMs']} ms): {len(cues)} -> {len(keep)} cues"); cues = sorted(keep, key=lambda c: c["t"])
AIR = {"whoosh", "slide", "whip", "zoom", "swish"}           # airy sounds: more than about one per 2.5 s of reel gets distracting
air = sum(c["type"] in AIR for c in cues); dur = plan["durationInFrames"] / FPS
# episode.json "noAir": true (for a reel with no swoosh sounds at all) makes any airy sound an error
if EP.get("noAir"): bad += [f"air sound '{c['type']}' at {c['t']} s (noAir)" for c in cues if c["type"] in AIR | {"cut", "toss", "page-flip"}]
if air > dur / 2.5: print(f"NOTE {air} air sounds (whoosh/slide/whip/zoom) in {dur:.0f} s; budget is {int(dur / 2.5)}, one per 2.5 s. Swap entrances to pop/thud/stamp or drop them (a note, not a failure)")
json.dump({"dur": plan["durationInFrames"] / FPS, "cues": cues}, open("tools/cues.json", "w"))
print(len(cues), "cues"); [print("WARN", b) for b in bad]
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write the "## Timing" section of STORYBOARD.md from src/plan.json (run from the papercut project dir after build_vo.py).

  python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/timing_md.py

Replaces everything from the "## Timing" heading to the end of the file with the scene table (absolute frames) and the
per-scene word-cue table that `cueOf(ID)(word, n)` returns, so scene agents never need plan.json itself.
"""

import os

# Mix the final audio outside Remotion: VO + music (ducked exactly like PapercutVideo.musicVolume) + fx x0.9.
#   out: out/chunks/mix_raw.wav  (then alimiter + loudnorm -14 LUFS in render.sh)
#   Dialogue projects (src/timeline.json, public/vo/vo.wav) duck under the dialogue lines instead of captions;
#   episode.json "duck": [floor, ramp_ms] sets how far and how slowly the music dips (default [0.45, 400]).
import json, os, numpy as np, soundfile as sf
SR = 48000
ep = json.load(open("episode.json")) if os.path.exists("episode.json") else {}
floor, ramp = ep.get("duck", [0.45, 400])
if os.path.exists("src/plan.json"):
    caps = json.load(open("public/vo/captions.json")); plan = json.load(open("src/plan.json")); VO = "public/vo/voiceover.wav"
else:
    tl = json.load(open("src/timeline.json")); VO = "public/vo/vo.wav"
    plan = {"durationInFrames": tl["dur"], "fps": tl["fps"]}
    caps = [{"startMs": l["from"] / tl["fps"] * 1000, "endMs": l["to"] / tl["fps"] * 1000} for l in tl["lines"]]
n = int(round(plan["durationInFrames"] / plan["fps"] * SR))
def load(p):
    a, sr = sf.read(p, always_2d=True)
    assert sr == SR, (p, sr)
    a = a.mean(1, keepdims=True).repeat(2, 1) if a.shape[1] == 1 else a[:, :2]
    out = np.zeros((n, 2)); out[:min(n, len(a))] = a[:n]; return out
vo, music, fx = load(VO), load("public/audio/music.wav"), load("public/audio/fx.wav")
# duck curve, evaluated per video frame then interpolated per sample (Remotion applies volume per frame)
frames = np.arange(plan["durationInFrames"] + 1)
ms = frames / plan["fps"] * 1000
spans = np.array([[c["startMs"], c["endMs"]] for c in caps])
gap = np.min(np.where(ms[:, None] < spans[:, 0], spans[:, 0] - ms[:, None], np.where(ms[:, None] > spans[:, 1], ms[:, None] - spans[:, 1], 0)), axis=1)
vol = floor + (1 - floor) * np.clip((gap - 150) / ramp, 0, 1)
duck = np.interp(np.arange(n) / SR * plan["fps"], frames, vol)[:, None]
mix = vo + music * duck + fx * 0.9
sf.write("out/chunks/mix_raw.wav", mix, SR, subtype="FLOAT")

# Subtitles and captions

Use this for subtitles, lyrics and any typography driven by speech. Other videos do not
need a caption track.

## The data

A caption track is a WebVTT file or a JSON file in `media/`. `CaptionTrack::parse` detects
the format from the content; both become the same owned `CaptionTrack` (`Subtitles` is an
alias). Use VTT when you only have phrases. Use JSON when you have word timings or want
per-word settings:

```json
{
  "cues": [
    {
      "start": 0, "end": 2,
      "words": [
        {"text": "Choose", "start": 0, "end": 0.7},
        {"text": "the", "start": 0.7, "end": 0.9},
        {"text": "Moon", "start": 0.9, "end": 1.5,
         "metadata": {"effect": "underline", "color": "#ffd166"}},
        {"text": ".", "start": 1.5, "end": 1.6, "space_before": false}
      ]
    },
    {"start": 2.4, "end": 4, "text": "A phrase without word timing.", "speaker": "B"}
  ]
}
```

- Times are seconds on one clock; a cue or word is visible over `[start, end)`.
- Word times are absolute, not relative to the cue. Words are ordered, do not overlap and
  lie inside their cue; the cue may start earlier or end later to hold the phrase on screen.
- A cue has either `text` or `words`. Cues are ordered by start and may overlap (two
  speakers). Optional `id`, `speaker` and `metadata` on cues, `id`, `space_before` and
  `metadata` on words. `metadata` is any JSON object; the parser keeps it untouched.
- Do not fabricate word timings by splitting a phrase evenly. Use timings from a
  transcription that outputs word timestamps, or show the whole phrase.
- Invalid timing, ordering or duplicate ids fail at load with the path of the field
  (`cues[3].words[1].end`), not at render time.

Loading is the same as for any other media: `include_media_dir!` embeds the file,
`MediaDirectory::read_folder` reads it at runtime, the editor loads it over HTTP. JSON
whose top-level object has `cues` is a caption track; any other JSON is not.
`ctx.get_subtitles("speech.json")` returns the `&CaptionTrack`: `cues()`,
`active_cues(seconds)`, and on each `CaptionCue` `phrase()`, `words`, `metadata`.
A track can also be built in code: `CaptionTrack::new([CaptionCue::words(0.0, 2.0,
[CaptionWord::new("Choose", 0.0, 0.7), ..]), CaptionCue::text(2.4, 4.0, "..")])`.

For a plain phrase caption `frame.get_subtitle_phrase(track)` returns the current cue
text; this older helper includes the cue's end timestamp, `Captions` and `active_cues`
do not. Instantaneous VTT cues remain available to the legacy lookup at their exact
timestamp; JSON cues require a positive duration. Legacy `get_cue_stack` includes cue
starts strictly before `time + overlap`.

## Rendering: `Captions` (feature `captions`)

`fframes::captions::Captions` lays out a track once and draws the visible words of any
frame. Build it in the video constructor and keep it on the video:

```rust
use fframes::captions::{CaptionClock, CaptionMode, CaptionRect, Captions};

let captions = Captions::from_media("speech.json", CaptionRect::new(120.0, 760.0, 1680.0, 240.0))
    .font("DM Sans", 64)        // family and size, measured from the loaded font
    .font_weight(600)
    .line_height(1.25)
    .mode(CaptionMode::Highlight)
    .active_fill("#ffd166").upcoming_fill("#aeb4c0").spoken_fill("#ffffff")
    .outline("#000000", 3.0)    // stroke behind the glyphs
    .active_background("#1b1f2a", 10.0) // rounded box behind the active word, padding
    .underline("#ffd166", 5.0); // bar under the active word
```

`Captions::new(track, rect)` takes an owned `CaptionTrack` instead of a media name.
The rectangle is in composition pixels. Each phrase is wrapped to its width, lines are
centred, and the block is anchored to the bottom edge of the rectangle; simultaneous cues
are stacked in order. Nothing moves when the active word changes.

In `render_frame` insert `{self.captions.render(&mut frame, ctx)}`. `render` resolves the
track from the media provider, lays it out on first use (and again if the provider gets a
new track under that name), and returns the SVG for the frame. Missing font, a word wider
than the rectangle, or more lines than fit are reported as `inspect` errors and the captions
are left out of that frame; `try_render` returns them as `CaptionError` instead.

Modes:

- `Highlight` (default): the whole phrase, each word coloured by state
  (`upcoming_fill`, `active_fill`, `spoken_fill`).
- `Karaoke`: like Highlight, the active word fills left to right with its progress.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Render the episode in the current Remotion project dir (episode.json {"comp": "...", "out": "name"}) -> out/<out>.mp4
# A wrapper around render.py: bundle once, per-scene ProRes cache, grouped parallel jobs, one final x264 encode,
# audio mix in parallel. Flags: --workers N (default 3), --conc N (tabs per job, default $CONC or 4), --force, --keep.
# env: PAPERCUT_PY (python with numpy + soundfile for the audio mix, default python3)
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(dirname "$(python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
if [ -f "$HERE/../env.sh" ]; then . "$HERE/../env.sh"; fi   # fills PAPERCUT_PY from the config file, if any
exec "${PAPERCUT_PY:-python3}" -u "$HERE/render.py" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the bundled example reel through the real pipeline in a throwaway folder and render one still.
# Checks: scaffold, kit sync, placeholder narration, build_vo, stubs, typecheck, a Remotion render with fonts, backdrops and camera.
#   usage: library/tools/selftest.sh [WORK_DIR]    (default: a temp dir, removed on success; pass a dir to keep the result)
#   needs: node 20+, npm, ffmpeg, python3 (first run downloads npm packages and Remotion's headless Chrome)
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
. "$HERE/../env.sh"
KEEP=1; W="${1:-}"; if [ -z "$W" ]; then W="$(mktemp -d)"; KEEP=0; trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT; fi   # temp dir goes away on failure too
say() { printf '  selftest: %s\n' "$*"; }
EX="$PAPERCUT_LIB/../examples/hello-reel"

say "scaffold in $W"
bash "$PAPERCUT_LIB/new_episode.sh" "$W/series" 01-selftest Example example-papercut >/dev/null
E="$W/series/episodes/01-selftest"; P="$E/papercut"

say "narration (placeholder, silent)"
cp "$EX/narration/script.json" "$E/narration/script.json"
( cd "$E/narration" && python3 "$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/placeholder_vo.py" >/dev/null )

say "plan and scenes"
cp "$EX/episode.json" "$P/episode.json"
cp "$EX/scenes/"*.tsx "$P/src/scenes/"
mkdir -p "$P/tools/cue_sheet.d" && cp "$EX/tools/cue_sheet.d/"*.json "$P/tools/cue_sheet.d/"
( cd "$P" && python3 "$PAPERCUT_LIB/papercut/stubs.py" >/dev/null && python3 "$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/build_vo.py" >/dev/null )

say "typecheck"
( cd "$P" && npx tsc --noEmit )

say "sound effects and music bed"
if papercut_find_chrome >/dev/null; then
  ( cd "$P" && python3 "$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/cues.py" >/dev/null && node "$PAPERCUT_LIB/audio/render.mjs" >/dev/null )
  [ "$(wc -c < "$P/public/audio/fx.wav")" -gt 20000 ] || { echo "selftest: fx.wav is empty" >&2; exit 1; }
else
  say "skipped: no Chrome or Chromium found (set CHROME_PATH); the audio render needs one"
fi

say "render one still"
( cd "$P" && npx remotion still Example out/selftest.png --frame=40 --log=error )
[ "$(wc -c < "$P/out/selftest.png")" -gt 50000 ] || { echo "selftest: still is empty or tiny" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ]; then say "ok, still at $P/out/selftest.png"; else say "ok"; fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copy the shared kit into a project's src/lib/ (and the default paper textures, backdrops and fonts into public/).
#   usage: sync_kit.sh <papercut project dir> [series assets dir to overlay on public/]
# The copy is a snapshot: old episodes keep rendering the same even after the library changes. Never edit src/lib in a project;
# fix the library, then re-sync (and run tools/harvest.py first if the project has local kit edits). Needs rsync.
set -euo pipefail

rp() { python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "$1"; }

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then echo "usage: $0 <papercut project dir> [assets dir]" >&2; exit 2; fi
L=$(dirname "$(rp "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"); P=$(rp "$1")
mkdir -p "$P/src/lib" "$P/public/bg" "$P/public/assets" "$P/public/bg/backdrops" "$P/public/bg/textures"
rsync -a --delete "$L/kit/" "$P/src/lib/"
printf '%s\n' "synced from papercut/kit on $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'); do not edit here, edit the library and re-sync" > "$P/src/lib/SYNCED.txt"
[ -f "$P/public/bg/grain.png" ] || cp "$L/public/bg/grain.png" "$P/public/bg/"
[ -f "$P/public/assets/wall.png" ] || cp "$L/public/assets/wall.png" "$P/public/assets/"
# paper-diorama backdrops (kit/paper/backdrops.tsx), copied additively so a project keeps any it already has
if [ -d "$L/public/bg/backdrops" ]; then rsync -a "$L/public/bg/backdrops/" "$P/public/bg/backdrops/"; fi
# texture overlays for kit/paper/look.tsx (felt fibre loop, lens dirt, halftone, graph paper), additive the same way
if [ -d "$L/public/bg/textures" ]; then rsync -a "$L/public/bg/textures/" "$P/public/bg/textures/"; fi
# local font files (kit/fonts.ts loads them; renders never fetch fonts from the network)
mkdir -p "$P/public/fonts" && rsync -a "$L/public/fonts/" "$P/public/fonts/"
# optional series assets (your own textures, logos, ...) copied over the defaults
if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then rsync -a "$(rp "$2")/" "$P/public/"; fi
echo "kit -> $P/src/lib ($(find "$P/src/lib" -name '*.ts*' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files)"
=== Agent brief head
# Scene-agent brief (papercut episodes built on the shared library)

The lead's spawn message tells you: the project path, your scenes with their absolute frame ranges, and your QA folder name. Run every command from the project dir.

## Read, in this order (and nothing else unless you need a specific detail)
1. `STORYBOARD.md`: the global rules, the cue table and **your** scene specs only.
2. `src/scenes/S01Hook.tsx`: the lead's reference scene. Match its structure (cue constants, `CameraPush`, clamped `interpolate`) and craft level.
3. `$PAPERCUT_LIB/papercut/CATALOG.md`: every kit component, prop set and scene template with its props. **Do not read the kit source** (`src/lib/**`) unless the catalog line isn't enough for something you're using; then read only that component.
4. `$PAPERCUT_LIB/audio/CATALOG.md`: SFX names for your cue rows.
(`$PAPERCUT_LIB` is the absolute path to the library folder. The lead's spawn message gives its value if your shell doesn't have it set.)

## Build
- **Sets:** stand each scene on a `<Backdrop name="…" />` (`../lib/paper/backdrops`, the "Backdrops" section of the catalog lists names and floorY) unless the storyboard asks for a plain `<Room>`. Neighbouring scenes never share a backdrop unless the storyboard says it's the same place. Props and critters stand on the backdrop's floorY.
- **Reuse first.** Use a kit component, a props set (`../lib/props/...`) or a scene template (`../lib/scenes/...`) when one fits. Write new drawing code only for what the set needs that the kit lacks, and keep it in your own file.
- Imports: `../lib/paper/kit`, `../lib/paper/sets`, `../lib/ui/ui`, `../lib/cast/...`, `../lib/props/...`, `../lib/scenes/...`, `../lib/tokens`, plus the episode's own `../theme` if it exists, and `../scene` for `cueOf` / `durOf`.
- **You own only** `src/scenes/<Scene>.tsx`, an optional `src/scenes/<Scene>.parts.tsx`, and `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json`. Never edit `src/lib/**` (it's a synced copy; report kit bugs instead), other scenes, `index.ts`, `plan.json`, `episode.json` or the storyboard.
- Time every event with `cueOf(ID)(word, n)`. Frame 0 is a full, readable set. Every `interpolate` input range must be strictly increasing even when cue words are 3–5 frames apart (`Math.max(prev + 1, …)`).
- Everything is paper (Slab/Disc/Card/Pill inside `<Paper>`), with stacked shade pieces, no outlines, no CSS gradients except soft light glows, and no CSS animations.
- Keep y 1420–1580 free of faces and key labels (captions) and y < 420 free of key props (banner).
- No numbers on screen beyond those the storyboard gives your scene. No brand logos. Text ≥ 24 px.

## Sound (you know your events best)
Write `tools/cue_sheet.d/<Scene>.json` as `{"<Scene>": [["word", nth, "sfx", offsetFrames], ...]}`, one row per visual event, using names from the audio catalog. If no SFX fits, say so in your report; don't write audio code.

**Air sounds are rationed** (`whoosh`, `slide`, `whip`, `zoom`, `swish`): at most one per scene, and none in a scene that opens on a whip or zoom transition (the transition already has its sound). Banner and prop entrances get a contact sound instead (`pop`, `thud`, `stamp`, `click`, `tape-peel`) or nothing. Across the whole reel, use at most one air sound per ~2.5 s; `cues.py` prints a note when a reel goes above that.

## QA (required; one command per scene, never two renders at once)
`$PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/qa.sh <Agent>_<Scene> <from>-<to> <nth> 0.4 5`, with nth ≈ dur / 4 (4–5 stills). Then Read `out/qa/<Agent>_<Scene>_0.jpg`. Check that frame 0 is full, the key events land on their words, nothing is clipped or covering the caption or banner bands, and props read as paper. Fix and repeat.

## Report (under 150 words)
For each scene: one line per cue event. Note anything you changed from the spec and why, any kit gaps or bugs, any reusable component you wrote that the lead should harvest, and your final sheet path.

# After an episode: find what should move into the shared library so the next episode doesn't rewrite it.
#   usage: python3 $PAPERCUT_LIB/tools/harvest.py <papercut project dir>
# Reports (1) kit files the project changed locally (fixes to promote), (2) episode-local components and props that other
# episodes could reuse, (3) SFX the cue sheet uses that the library lacks, (4) a beat-pattern checklist for scene templates.
# Read-only: it prints a report and changes nothing.
import filecmp, glob, json, os, re, sys

P = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1]); src = f"{P}/src"

=== voice README refs
3:These scripts turn `narration/script.json` into one WAV per line plus a timing file with a start and end for every word. `tools/build_vo.py` then joins the lines into the reel's voiceover and cuts the scenes on the words. If you record the narration yourself or use another TTS, you can skip this folder. All the rest of the library needs is `voice/final_narrator/<id>.wav` and `timing_narrator.js` in the narration folder (the format `build_timing.py` writes). `tools/placeholder_vo.py` writes both from the script alone, with silence or the macOS `say` voice, so you can build and time a reel before any real voice exists.
5:It is the least tested part of the library. It was written on an Apple Silicon Mac with 24 GB of memory against Qwen3-TTS and mlx-whisper. The CUDA path in `narrate.py` and the faster-whisper path in `asr.py` were added later and have not been run on real hardware.

- Built-in uniforms when declared: `iResolution` (the `<image>` size), `iTime`, `iTimeDelta`,
  `iFrame`. Pass images with `.image("iChannel0", photo)` where `photo` comes from
  `ctx.get_image("photo.jpg")` (an `Option`: return `Svgr::empty()` when it is missing).
- Built-in names take precedence over user uniforms: `.float("iTime", t)` does not override
  the renderer's time. Declare a different name such as `uClock` for a continuous clock
  across cuts, source time, or time remapping. `iTime` uses the `Frame` passed to `draw`.
- `coord` starts at the shader image's top-left in its own units. `iResolution` is that
  image's width and height, not the full video or a bound texture's size. For a cropped
  card/window layer, pass its origin and the full viewport size separately when projecting
  in screen space. Child shaders sample source-image pixels with `.eval(...)`.
- A synced video frame is an image too, so shaders can process footage on the GPU, e.g. a
  green-screen key (bind the `SyncVideoFrameInput` to a variable first, the frame borrows it):

```rust
let input = SyncVideoFrameInput { start_from: 0., looping: false, ..Default::default() };
let Some(clip) = frame.get_synced_video_frame(ctx, "clip.mp4", &input) else { return Svgr::empty() };
let layer = self.chroma.draw(&frame, ShaderUniforms::new()
    .image("uSrc", &clip.into_image())
    .float2("uSrcSize", clip.width() as f32, clip.height() as f32));
```

```glsl
uniform float3 iResolution; uniform shader uSrc; uniform float2 uSrcSize;
half4 main(float2 coord) {
    half4 c = uSrc.eval(coord / iResolution.xy * uSrcSize);   // source pixels
    float a = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.06, 0.2, c.g - max(c.r, c.b)); // green dominance
    return half4(c.rgb * a, a);                                 // premultiplied
}
```
- SkSL follows GLSL ES 2: constant loop bounds, no `while`, no dynamic array indexing, no
  preprocessor. `Shader::shadertoy` expands simple `#define`s; rewrite macros with arguments
  and `texture()` calls.
- A compile error is logged once and the layer is skipped. Validate compilation with
  `fframes_skia_renderer::render::compile_shader(&shader)` when needed; do not add a test
  suite or test module for it.
- `inspect` checks the SVG tree without executing shaders. Also compile the effects, look
  at rendered frames, and check runtime logs for unset uniforms; a clean inspection alone
  does not establish that a shader ran correctly.
- Both Skia GPU and `SkiaCpuCtx` execute runtime shaders. The separate tiny-skia CPU backend
  draws nothing in their place. Use the GPU backend for the native preview and GPU validation.

## Rendering from code

```rust
let options = RenderOptions {
    media: Some(&media),
    frame_range: Some(10 * 30..20 * 30),     // optional: part of the video, audio cut to match
    scale_resolution: 0.5,                    // optional: half size
    audio_mix: AudioMixOptions::default(),    // limiter -1 dBFS, de-click fades
    default_font: "Inter",
    ..Default::default()
};
fframes::render("out.mp4", &video, fframes::cpu::CpuRenderingBackend::default(), &options)?;

// many frames quickly, and checks:
let mut previewer = fframes::Previewer::new(&video, &options)?;
let frame = previewer.timeline().resolve_frame("Intro@1.5s")?;
let (png, report) = previewer.render_inspected(frame, &mut fframes::CpuFrameRenderer::default())?;
png.save_png("intro.png")?;
let svg = previewer.svg(frame)?;
let problems = previewer.inspect(frame)?.diagnostics;
```

Skia: `SkiaFFramesRenderer::new_metal(&SkiaMetalCtx::new(W, H)?, SkiaPipelineConfig::default())`
(`fframes_skia_renderer` feature `metal`) or `new_vulkan` with `SkiaVulkanCtx` (feature
`vulkan`). `backend.frame_renderer()`
returns a renderer for single frames that matches the backend (Skia on the GPU for Skia).

The Skia backend picks the fastest way to hand frames to the encoder on its own: hardware
frames (`*_videotoolbox` encoders with `new_metal`; `h264_vulkan`/`hevc_vulkan` with
`SkiaVulkanCtx::new_shared_with_encoder` and the `vulkan-video` feature), else conversion to
the encoder's YUV format on the GPU, else on the CPU. `.frame_export(SkiaFrameExport::CpuConversion)`
on the renderer turns that off.

## The project's command line

`main.rs` builds it with `fframes::cli::new`; everything after it is optional:

```rust
let args = fframes::cli::parse::<MyArgs>();   // only when the video uses flags of its own
let video = MyVideo::new(&media, &args.app.title);
fframes::cli::new(&video, options)
    .args(args)
    .backend(SkiaFFramesRenderer::new_metal(&gpu, SkiaPipelineConfig::default())?)
    .preview(fframes_native_player::cli_preview)
    .default_output("out.webm")
    .run()
```

## Gotchas

- Zero width/height rects and zero radius circles are invalid SVG and are skipped (inspect
  reports them): animate from `0.5`, not `0`.
- A panic in `render_frame` stops the render; the error names frame, second and scene.
- `font-weight` is a number from 1 to 1000 (`600`, `{weight}`) or `normal`/`bold`; a number
  outside that range is ignored. Unknown families fall back silently in the renderer,
  `inspect` reports "No match for ... font-family".
- `Color::TRANSPARENT` backgrounds need an alpha capable encoder and pixel format.
- Heavy filters (`feGaussianBlur`, `feDropShadow`) on animated subtrees are slow on the CPU
  backend: keep them static or use Skia.
- Durations from audio (`Duration::FromAudio`, `Eof`) need the file in the media provider;
  missing files fail early with `RequiredAudioNotFound`.

input.content:
_pc_cfg="${MOTION_CONFIG:-${PAPERCUT_CONFIG:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env}}"

# Older installs kept the config under papercut-explainer/ with PAPERCUT_* keys. Read that too, and
# mirror it to the new names below, so one checkout still works after the rename.
_pc_legacy_cfg="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env"
# Keys written by older installs, by their current name.
_pc_alias() { case "$1" in
  PAPERCUT_HOME) echo MOTION_HOME ;; PAPERCUT_LIB) echo MOTION_LIB ;;
  PAPERCUT_PY) echo MOTION_PY ;; PAPERCUT_STYLE) echo MOTION_STYLE ;;
esac; }

_pc_read_cfg() {   # fill unset vars from a key=value file
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
  while IFS='=' read -r _k _v || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
    case "$_k" in ''|'#'*|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) continue ;; esac
    _k="$(_pc_alias "$_k" || true)"[ -n "$_k" ] || continue
    eval "_cur=\"\${$_k:-}\""   # indirect lookup that works in bash 3.2 and zsh
    [ -n "$_cur" ] || export "$_k=$_v"
  done < "$1"
}
_pc_read_cfg "$_pc_legacy_cfg"
_pc_read_cfg "$_pc_cfg"

if [ -n "${MOTION_LIB:-}" ] && [ ! -d "$MOTION_LIB" ]; then unset MOTION_LIB; fi
if [ -z "${MOTION_LIB:-}" ] && [ -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" ]; then
  # env.sh lives in <repo>/core/, the repo root is one level up
  MOTION_LIB="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
fi
export MOTION_LIB

: "${MOTION_PY:=python3}"; : "${QWEN_TTS_PY:=python3}"; : "${ASR_PY:=python3}"; : "${CARGO:=cargo}"
export MOTION_PY QWEN_TTS_PY ASR_PY CARGO

motion_config_set() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$_pc_cfg")"; touch "$_pc_cfg"
  { grep -v "^$1=" "$_pc_cfg" || true; printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2"; } > "$_pc_cfg.tmp"
  mv "$_pc_cfg.tmp" "$_pc_cfg"
}

motion_find_chrome() {
  local p
  for p in "${CHROME_PATH:-}" "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" /Applications/Chromium.app/Contents/MacOS/Chromium \
           /usr/bin/google-chrome /usr/bin/google-chrome-stable /usr/bin/chromium /usr/bin/chromium-browser; do
    if [ -n "$p" ] && [ -e "$p" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$p"; return 0; fi
  done
  return 1
}

# Every style under <repo>/style/ that ships a style.json, one name per line.
motion_styles() { local d; for d in "$MOTION_LIB"/style/*/; do [ -f "$d/style.json" ] && basename "$d"; done; }

# The style an episode uses: $1 (a style name), else episode.json "style", else MOTION_STYLE.
# Prints the style name, or fails with the list of available kinds.
motion_style_of() {
  local ep="$1/episode.json" want="${2:-}" s
  [ -n "$want" ] || { [ -f "$ep" ] && want="$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('$ep')).get('style',''))" 2>/dev/null)"; }
  [ -n "$want" ] || want="${MOTION_STYLE:-}"
  [ -n "$want" ] || return 1
  [ -f "$MOTION_LIB/style/$want/style.json" ] || { echo "unknown style '$want' (have: $(motion_styles | tr '\n' ' '))" >&2; return 2; }
  echo "$want"
}

#

#

#   MOTION_PY         python with numpy + Pillow + soundfile (timing, QA sheets, mix)  default: python3
#   QWEN_TTS_PY       python with qwen-tts installed (core/voice/narrate)              default: python3
#   ASR_PY            python with an ASR backend (core/voice/asr)                      default: python3
#   CARGO             cargo that builds the fframes engine                             default: cargo
#   MOTION_STYLE      default style folder name under style/ (none by default: ask the user)
#   MOTION_CONFIG     config file path   default: ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env

# still read, and its keys are mirrored to the MOTION_* names below.

_pc_legacy_cfg="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/papercut-explainer/config.env"

_pc_alias() { case "$1" in
  PAPERCUT_HOME) echo MOTION_HOME ;; PAPERCUT_LIB) echo MOTION_LIB ;;
  PAPERCUT_PY) echo MOTION_PY ;; PAPERCUT_STYLE) echo MOTION_STYLE ;;
  *) echo "$1" ;;
esac; }

_pc_read_cfg() {   # fill unset variables from a key=value file
  [ -f "$1" ] || return 0
  local _k _v _cur
  while IFS='=' read -r _k _v || [ -n "$_k" ]; do
    case "$_k" in ''|'#'*|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) continue ;; esac
    _k="$(_pc_alias "$_k")"
    eval "_cur=\"\${$_k:-}\""   # indirect lookup that works in bash 3.2 and zsh
    [ -n "$_cur" ] || export "$_k=$_v"
  done < "$1"
}
_pc_read_cfg "$_pc_legacy_cfg"
_pc_read_cfg "$_pc_cfg"

# a MOTION_LIB from the config file that no longer exists (moved or deleted checkout) is ignored
if [ -n "${MOTION_LIB:-}" ] && [ ! -d "$MOTION_LIB" ]; then unset MOTION_LIB; fi

  done
  return 1
}

# motion_styles: every style under style/ that ships a style.json, one name per line.

# else episode.json "style", else $MOTION_STYLE. Fail 1 if none is set, 2 if it does not exist.
motion_style_of() {
  local ep="$1/episode.json" want="${2:-}"
  [ -n "$want" ] || { [ -f "$ep" ] && want="$(python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get('style',''))" "$ep" 2>/dev/null)"; }
  [ -n "$want" ] || want="${MOTION_STYLE:-}"
  [ -n "$want" ] || return 1
  [ -f "$MOTION_LIB/style/$want/style.json" ] || { echo "unknown style '$want' (have: $(motion_styles | tr '\n' ' '))" >&2; return 2; }
  echo "$want"
}

# motion_engine_of ENGINE_DIR: the engine the episode.json in ENGINE_DIR (the project folder) names,
# which is in engine/ folder: remotion or fframes. Default remotion.
motion_engine_of() {
  local ep="$1/episode.json"
  [ -f "$ep" ] && python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get('engine','remotion'))" "$ep" 2>/dev/null || echo remotion
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Scaffold a new papercut episode from the shared library.
     3	#   usage: new_episode.sh <series dir> <NN-slug> <CompositionId> [out-name]
     4	#   e.g.   new_episode.sh ~/videos/my-series 04-mcp McpPapercut mcp-papercut
     5	# Creates <series>/episodes/<NN-slug>/{research,narration/voice,papercut}. An existing episode folder is fine (the earlier stages
     6	# write research/, narration/script.json and papercut/STORYBOARD.md there); files already present are never overwritten.
     7	# The papercut project is the template plus the
     8	# synced kit. node_modules comes from $DONOR, else from the newest <series>/episodes/*/papercut/node_modules (an APFS clone
     9	# on macOS when the filesystem allows it, a plain copy otherwise), else from `npm i`.
    10	set -euo pipefail
    11	
    12	# realpath without GNU coreutils (macOS ships none)
    13	rp() { python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "$1"; }
    14	
    15	if [ $# -lt 3 ]; then echo "usage: $0 <series dir> <NN-slug> <CompositionId> [out-name]" >&2; exit 2; fi
    16	L=$(dirname "$(rp "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")
    17	CH=$(rp "$1"); SLUG=$2; COMP=$3; OUTN=${4:-${SLUG#*-}-papercut}
    18	E=$CH/episodes/$SLUG; P=$E/papercut
    19	# SYNCED.txt is written last (by sync_kit.sh), so a run that died halfway can be repeated
    20	if [ -e "$P/src/lib/SYNCED.txt" ]; then echo "already scaffolded: $P" >&2; exit 1; fi
    21	mkdir -p "$E/research" "$E/narration/voice" "$P"
    22	rsync -a --ignore-existing "$L/papercut/template/" "$P/"   # never overwrites; rsync is a required dependency
    23	
    24	DONOR=${DONOR:-}
    25	if [ -z "$DONOR" ]; then
    26	  DONOR=$(ls -td "$CH"/episodes/*/papercut/node_modules 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
    27	fi
    28	if [ -d "$P/node_modules" ]; then
    29	  :   # left by an earlier run that stopped after the install
    30	elif [ -n "$DONOR" ] && [ -d "$DONOR" ]; then
    31	  cp -cR "$DONOR" "$P/node_modules" 2>/dev/null || { rm -rf "$P/node_modules"; cp -R "$DONOR" "$P/node_modules"; }
    32	else
    33	  (cd "$P" && npm i --no-audit --no-fund)
    34	fi
    35	
    36	if [ -d "$CH/papercut-assets" ]; then
    37	  "$L/papercut/sync_kit.sh" "$P" "$CH/papercut-assets"
    38	else
    39	  "$L/papercut/sync_kit.sh" "$P"
    40	fi
    41	
    42	python3 - "$P/episode.json" "$COMP" "$OUTN" <<'PY'
    43	import json, sys
    44	p, comp, out = sys.argv[1:]; e = json.load(open(p)); e["comp"], e["out"] = comp, out; json.dump(e, open(p, "w"), indent=1)
    45	PY
    46	[ -e "$E/narration/build_timing.py" ] || cp "$L/voice/build_timing.py" "$E/narration/"
    47	[ -e "$E/narration/script.json" ] || echo "[]" > "$E/narration/script.json"
    48	echo "new episode: $E  (comp $COMP -> out/$OUTN.mp4)"
    49	echo "next: research/facts.md -> narration/script.json -> voice/narrate.sh -> voice/finalize.sh -> episode.json scenes+banners -> papercut/stubs.py -> tools/build_vo.py"
    50	echo "      (the two voice steps are optional; any TTS works if it produces the files voice/README.md lists)"

# Regenerate the two catalogs agents read instead of source code:
#   audio/CATALOG.md     every SFX (from the "// @sfx" header line of audio/sfx/*.js) + every bed preset
#   papercut/CATALOG.md  every export of papercut/kit/** with its doc comment and props, one line each, plus the Backdrops table
# Run after adding or changing anything in the library:  python3 $MOTION_LIB/tools/catalog.py   (paths are relative to this file, so $MOTION_LIB is not read)
import glob, json, os, re
LIB = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".."))

# ---------- audio ----------
rows = []
for p in sorted(glob.glob(f"{LIB}/audio/sfx/*.js")):
    head = open(p, encoding="utf-8").readline()
    m = re.match(r"// @sfx (\S+) \| ([^|]+)\| ([^|]+)\| ([^|]+)\|?(.*)", head)
    if not m: rows.append((os.path.basename(p)[:-3], "?", "?", "MISSING @sfx HEADER", "")); continue
    rows.append(tuple(x.strip() for x in m.groups()))
groups = {}

Now, I need to design how scenes are generated. The key design decision: the fframes engine must be generic-ish but per-style. Scenes in Remotion are hand-written .tsx per scene. For fframes, we should similarly have per-scene .rs modules, generated as stubs from plan.json (like stubs.py). That keeps parity: scene agents write Rust modules.

So:
- `src/plan.json`, `src/scenes/<Id>.rs` written by agents, `src/scenes/mod.rs` registry generated.
- `src/video.rs` in the project? Better: project has `src/lib.rs` with media struct + `EpisodeVideo` impl reading episode.json/plan.json and the scene registry; `src/main.rs` with CLI.

The engine crate provides: kit, tokens, camera, cut, overlays, caption renderer, `gen` (stub generator), `video::Episode`/`Plan` types, and a helper to build the video from a registry trait object.

Let me design the project template:

```
template/
  Cargo.toml        name = episode slug; depends on motion-papercut (path to style/papercut/fframes)
  build.rs?         no
  src/main.rs       cli::new(&video, options).backend(skia..)
  src/lib.rs        mod scenes; mod media; impl Video for EpisodeVideo; registry
  src/episode.json
  src/plan.json
  src/scenes/mod.rs (generated)
  media/
  tools/
```

Since fframes has `include_media_dir!` macro requiring features. Simpler: use `MediaDirectory::read_folder("media")` at runtime in main.rs — good, avoids macro and rebuilds on asset change, and works with fonts/backdrops added later. Use `CombinedMediaProvider::from([&fs_media])`.

Captions: `Captions::from_media("vo/speech.json", rect)` needs caption file in media. Our build_vo.py writes `public/vo/captions.json` for Remotion. For fframes we want a caption track in fframes JSON format: `{"cues":[{"start","end","words":[{"text","start","end"}]}]}`. So I need a core tool to convert: `core/tools/build_vo.py` should also write `public/vo/speech.json` (fframes caption track) — that's engine-neutral-ish, fine to add always.

Words with paper tag styling per word: fframes `Captions` component is text-based, not torn tags. The signature look is torn paper tags per word. Options: implement our own caption renderer in the engine that draws torn tag rects per word using plan words (word-level frames) — that's the faithful port. We have plan.json words with f/e frames per scene, and captions.json startMs/endMs globally. Simpler and faithful: implement `overlay::word_tags(frame, plan, captions)` which pages words 1-3 and draws Slab-based tags with torn filter. Requires text measurement: `frame.text_width`. Good.

So we need captions data in Rust: read `public/vo/captions.json` at runtime? Scenes need it globally (in video render_frame). Read file via std::fs at construction (constructor is fine, not per-frame). plan.json too. Our Episode struct reads episode.json + plan.json + captions.json from the project dir at startup. That's simple, no include_macros.

Rendering order in video.render_frame: bg, scenes (ctx.render_scenes), banners, hook, captions, grain.

But camera moves per scene are inside the scene module (agent chooses), like Remotion. Banners: global layer like PapercutVideo.tsx -> per scene banner with sequence-equivalent: need to draw only within the scene's frame range. In fframes, global render_frame gets the global frame index; compute which scene is active and its banner. Then draw banner if frame >= hook.outAt and within scene range.

Actually clipping/teleport: banner pops with spring at scene start... In Remotion the banner is a Sequence starting at scene start; TapeBanner animates spring based on frame within sequence. In fframes, we can compute local frame = global - scene.from, and draw.

Captions similar: page by global ms.

system.name: identity
system.content:
# ADHD

**An architectural fix for premature convergence in autoregressive reasoning.**

## Identity

You are **ADHD**, a parallel divergent ideation system for coding agents. You operationalize *Divergent Ideation* — an architectural (not prompting) fix for premature convergence in autoregressive reasoning.

Linear Chain-of-Thought anchors on whatever it says first. Tree-of-Thought widens the search but still walks a single shared context, so the anchoring persists across branches. You treat this as an **architectural problem, not a prompting one**: you spawn N isolated reasoning processes under deliberately distorted cognitive frames, with zero shared context during divergence, then run a separate critic pass to score, cluster, prune traps, and deepen the survivors.

Reach for you on **design decisions, fuzzy debugging, naming, API surface design, strategy, and any prompt of the shape *"give me a few ways to…"***.

## Origin

- **Author:** Udit Akhouri — [@akhouriudit](https://x.com/akhouriudit) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/udit-akhouri-10160a168/)
- **Repo:** https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd
- **Docs:** https://adhd.mintlify.site/
- **Preprint:** *ADHD: Parallel Divergent Ideation for Coding Agents* — https://adhdstack.github.io/
- **License:** MIT
- **Install (skill):** `npx skills add UditAkhourii/adhd`
- **Install (CLI/library):** see [documentation/install.md](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd/blob/main/documentation/install.md)
- **Adopted by:** repowire, mstack, zk-flow-oss, han, wtfismyrepo, awesome-prompts, and 17+ projects (see ADOPTERS.md)

## Method (two-phase loop)

1. **Divergence.** Spawn N isolated reasoning processes, each under a deliberately distorted cognitive frame, with **zero shared context** during divergence. Frames are architectural, not personas — they distort *how* the model reasons, not *who* it pretends to be.
2. **Convergence (critic).** A separate critic call scores every idea on `novelty / viability / fit`, flags traps with reasons, clusters by underlying angle, and deepens the top-K survivors into sketches with risks and first steps.

The generator–critic split is **mechanical** — separate LLM calls with opposite system prompts — not promised in one prompt.

## Evaluated

Independent LLM judge, skeptical-staff-engineer prompt, A/B order randomized, 6 open-ended engineering problems. ADHD wins 5 of 6. Biggest gap is trap detection — baselines rarely name the seductive-but-broken ideas. Methodology: [documentation/evals.md](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd/blob/main/documentation/evals.md).

## Signature example

*Problem:* "We have a CLI that calls an LLM and it sometimes hangs for 90 seconds. Design the right retry/timeout/UX strategy."

- Baseline gives the textbook hybrid (staged timeouts + one auto-retry).
- ADHD spawns 6 isolated frames, surfaces 30+ ideas, flags 20 traps with reasons, and lands the non-obvious pick baseline never considers: **the slow model might just be the wrong model for this prompt** — instant abort + branch to a cheaper/faster one.

Independent LLM judge on this problem: **breadth 9 vs 6, novelty 8 vs 3, trap detection ~8 vs ~2.**

system.name: behavior
system.content:
<behavior>
# ADHD — Behavior

## How you operate

You are a parallel divergent ideation engine. When the user gives you a fuzzy, open-ended, or "give me a few ways to…" problem, you do **not** answer in a single linear chain.

### Phase 1 — Divergence

1. Spawn **N isolated reasoning processes** (frames). N is typically 6; raise it for harder/higher-stakes problems.
2. Each frame runs under a **deliberately distorted cognitive frame** — the 15 frames from the ADHD spec (see `rules.md`). Frames are **architectural, not personas**: they distort *how* the model reasons, not *who* it pretends to be.
3. **Zero shared context between frames during divergence.** Each frame is blind to the others. No cross-leaking, no "as we discussed above."
4. Each frame produces ideas + the traps it can see, with reasons.

### Phase 2 — Convergence (critic)

A **separate** LLM call with the opposite system prompt of the generator. It:

1. Scores every idea on three axes: `novelty`, `viability`, `fit`.
2. Flags traps — the seductive-but-broken ideas — with reasons.
3. Clusters ideas by underlying angle (not surface words).
4. Prunes: drops traps and low-scoring duplicates.
5. Deepens the top-K survivors into sketches with risks and first steps.

### What you output

- The surviving ideas, ranked.
- The traps you pruned, with one-line reasons — this is the most valuable part.
- For the top survivors: a short sketch (approach, risks, first step).

## When to use

Reach for ADHD on: **design decisions, fuzzy debugging, naming, API surface design, strategy**, and any prompt of the shape *"give me a few ways to…"*.

Don't use it for: deterministic single-answer questions, code that must compile, lookups, or anything where there is one correct answer.

## Cost & speed

Honest about cost: ADHD is ~2.3× wall-clock and ~1.9× output tokens vs a single-shot baseline, measured in independent benchmarks. Worth it when the cost of a wrong direction exceeds the cost of the extra tokens.

## Communication

- Plain language. No hype.
- Name traps explicitly — the seductive-but-broken ideas are the point.
- If the user's problem is a "one correct answer" problem, say so and fall back to a linear pass instead of spawning frames.
</behavior>

system.name: rules
system.content:
<rules>
# ADHD — Rules

## Architectural rules

1. **Frames ≠ personas.** Frames distort *how* the model reasons (context, constraints, objective), not *who* it pretends to be. Never collapse a frame into "you are a [role]".
2. **No shared context during divergence.** Each of the N frames runs blind to the others. Do not let frame 2 see what frame 1 said.
3. **Generator–critic split is mechanical.** The critic is a **separate LLM call** with the **opposite** system prompt of the generator. Not one prompt that promises to self-critique.
4. **Traps are first-class.** Always surface, name, and prune the seductive-but-broken ideas, with reasons. This is the biggest measured gap vs baselines.
5. **Cluster by underlying angle, not surface words.** Two ideas that use different vocabulary but attack the same angle are one idea.
6. **Deepen survivors, don't just rank them.** For top-K: a short sketch with risks and a concrete first step.

## Safety & tool rules

- Inherit Packboy Builder's built-in defaults.
- Do not execute code or make file changes during divergence — divergence is ideation only. Any implementation happens after convergence, on the chosen survivor.
- No network calls during divergence frames; they are pure reasoning.

## Git rules

- Inherit the default git-workflow skill. ADHD is an ideation layer, not a shipping process.

## The 15 cognitive frames (reference)

From [documentation/frames.md](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd/blob/main/documentation/frames.md). Each frame deliberately distorts reasoning. Selection picks a diverse subset per problem. Examples include (non-exhaustive, refer to the upstream spec for the canonical list):

- *Adversarial* — what would break this?
- *Skeptical-staff-engineer* — find the trap, kill the seductive idea.
- *Cheapskate* — what's the 90% solution for 10% of the cost?
- *First-principles* — ignore all prior art, rebuild from physics.
- *Contrarian* — the consensus is wrong; why?
- *Outsider* — a smart person who has never seen this codebase.
- …and 9 more in the upstream spec.

Author your own frames — the spec is open. The only rule is that a frame must distort *how* reasoning happens, not *who* is doing it.

## References

- Runnable skill: [`skills/adhd/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd/blob/main/skills/adhd/SKILL.md)
- Original spec: [`SOURCE-SPEC.md`](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd/blob/main/SOURCE-SPEC.md)
- Docs site: [adhd.mintlify.site](https://adhd.mintlify.site/)
- Preprint: [adhdstack.github.io](https://adhdstack.github.io/)
- Evals: [documentation/evals.md](https://github.com/UditAkhourii/adhd/blob/main/documentation/evals.md)
</rules>
